dimensions.summary:
I parsed every JSON-LD block in the existing build of HEAD a7aaedfc. That is 7,050 HTML files, of which 7,047 have JSON-LD; the 3 without it are redirect stubs. There are 14,093 blocks and 0 parse errors. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-blog/c0138ac4-51ee-5beb-a1c9-21d2311d0295/scratchpad/audit/structured-data/parse_ld.py.

The block set is the same on every template. Each page has one @graph with Organization, LocalBusiness and WebSite. All 6,257 posts add BlogPosting, and every page except the home page and redirect stubs adds one BreadcrumbList (7,046 pages). No page emits FAQPage, ItemList or CollectionPage.

All business values (name, telephone +84942467674, email, address, hours 09:00–21:00, priceRange 150000-200000 VND taken from pricing.yml) are identical on all 7,047 pages. They match _data/business.yml, data/business-facts.json, the visible footer, /gioi-thieu/, and the live Google Business Profile (GBP) and main site.

New issues found (none of these were in the earlier SEO waves):
1. **4 posts have invalid BreadcrumbList markup.** Item 3 has a null name and the item URL "https://blog…//"; item 4 has no item URL. The cause is parent_id P-AN-TOAN-PHAP-LY, which does not exist in factory-parents.yml.
2. **25 posts cut the visible breadcrumb label at the first " - "**, while the JSON-LD keeps the full title, so the two disagree.
3. **All 6,257 posts use the site logo as BlogPosting.image.** Google's Article guidance says not to use logos, and no post has its own image.
4. **254 published posts were revised with revise-published.py on 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-27, but none updated dateModified.** No post shows a visible "Cập nhật" (updated) date.
5. **LocalBusiness address and graph details:** the ward "Bồ Đề" is missing, the country is "Việt Nam" instead of "VN", hours are hard-coded, there is no hasMap or areaServed, BlogPosting.author has no url, and WebSite has no publisher.
6. **Two owner decisions:** whether to link the blog's business entity to the main site (thuexemaynguyentu.com), and the about.me profile in sameAs, whose text includes a forbidden "hơn 10 năm kinh nghiệm" claim.

SEO-106 (keep LocalBusiness/Organization on every page) re-checked: no new evidence, so it stays DECIDED_KEEP. Not adding FAQPage, ItemList, SearchAction or aggregateRating is correct.

I tested the proposed changes to the two template files (seo.html, article-breadcrumb.html) in a small throwaway site built in the audit folder from copies of the site data and five real post headers, not the real repo. The fixes produced valid, matching output there. Diffs are at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-blog/c0138ac4-51ee-5beb-a1c9-21d2311d0295/scratchpad/audit/structured-data/proposed/seo.html.diff and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-blog/c0138ac4-51ee-5beb-a1c9-21d2311d0295/scratchpad/audit/structured-data/proposed/article-breadcrumb.html.diff. A draft generator for the revision dates is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-blog/c0138ac4-51ee-5beb-a1c9-21d2311d0295/scratchpad/audit/structured-data/build_post_modified.py, and its output (254 posts) is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-blog/c0138ac4-51ee-5beb-a1c9-21d2311d0295/scratchpad/audit/structured-data/post-modified.json.

Live check: I used 1 TinyFish call. about.me and Pinterest are the business's own profiles (name/phone/address match). Facebook needed a login and TripAdvisor returned HTTP 403, so those two are UNKNOWN. The GBP page lists the website thuexemaynguyentu.com, hours 9AM–9PM, 38 reviews averaging 4.1, and a map pin; I did not use the pin or reviews for any proposal.

WebFetch could not reach developers.google.com (DNS blocked in this session). I read the Google guidance through the Parallel Search extract on 2026-10-31 instead.

The repo was not modified.

metrics.localbusiness_missing_props: postalCode, geo, hasMap, areaServed (ward 'Bồ Đề' omitted from streetAddress)

findings.title: BreadcrumbList invalid on 4 posts: null name and bad URL at position 3, missing item URL at position 4; visible trail has 3 levels
findings.evidence: check.py over the build: bcl.null_name=4, bcl.item_double_slash=4 (item 'https://blog.thuexemaynguyentu.com//'), bcl.no_item=4, bcl.len_mismatch[post]=4 (visible 3 items vs JSON-LD 5). Root cause: front matter parent_id 'P-AN-TOAN-PHAP-LY' (grep: exactly 4 posts, BLG-01381..01384) does not exist in _data/factory-parents.yml (the canonical key is P-PHAP-LY), while child_id resolves in factory-taxonomy.yml (e.g. C-BAO-HIEM, p: P-PHAP-LY). _includes/article-breadcrumb.html emits ListItem 3 and 4 regardless of whether bc_parent exists. CI misses it: scripts/factory/check-built-links.py extracts "item" strings by regex, so '//' resolves to the root and passes, and a null item is skipped; scripts/faq/faq_parity_check.py only checks that JSON parses.
findings.root_cause: article-breadcrumb.html does not guard JSON-LD positions 3 and 4 on bc_parent (the visible HTML does), and it has no fallback when parent_id is an unknown alias.
findings.proposed_fix:
In _includes/article-breadcrumb.html (diff: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-blog/c0138ac4-51ee-5beb-a1c9-21d2311d0295/scratchpad/audit/structured-data/proposed/article-breadcrumb.html.diff):
(1) After bc_child_node is assigned, add `{% if bc_parent == nil and bc_child_node %}{% assign bc_parent = site.data.factory-parents[bc_child_node.p] %}{% endif %}`, so the parent is derived from the child taxonomy without touching _posts/.
(2) Rewrite the JSON-LD so the parent and child ListItems are emitted only inside `{% if bc_parent %}` / `{% if bc_child_node %}`, with a running position counter. The last item then always takes the next position.
In the throwaway test build, the 4 posts render a 5-level trail (…> An toàn & pháp lý > Bảo hiểm xe máy > title) that is identical in the visible HTML and the JSON-LD; all item URLs exist in the build.
Apply the same child-to-parent fallback to art_parent_id in _layouts/post.html, which feeds related-articles.
Add a CI assertion: every non-last ListItem needs a non-empty name and an item URL, positions run 1..n, and JSON-LD names equal the visible breadcrumb. The audit script check.py can be adapted for this.
findings.rollback: git revert of the include/layout commit; output returns to the current bytes. No URL, canonical or post bytes change.
findings.benefit: Removes invalid breadcrumb items (missing required name/item) that would show as Breadcrumbs errors in Search Console. Restores hub links on 4 posts.
findings.verdict: IMPLEMENT_WITH_CHANGES: (a) The issue is real. Google's breadcrumb doc (https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/breadcrumb, fetched today) marks `name` and `position` as required on every ListItem and `item` as required on every ListItem except the last. These 4 pages have name:null plus a '//'

findings.title: Visible breadcrumb truncates 25 post titles at the first ' - ' (e.g. 'Từ vựng Việt'), while BreadcrumbList JSON-LD uses the full title
findings.evidence: check.py: bcl.name_mismatch[post]=25. Every post whose title contains ' - ' is affected: 25 such titles (grep _posts), and 0 post titles contain the site-title suffix. Example: visible 'Từ vựng Việt' vs JSON-LD/H1 'Từ vựng Việt - Anh khi nhận và trả xe máy thuê: xước, phanh, bình xăng'; 'Kinh nghiệm ghé thăm Văn Miếu' vs '… Văn Miếu - Quốc Tử Giám nửa ngày'. Cause: article-breadcrumb.html uses `page.title | split: ' - ' | first` for the visible item but `page.title` in JSON-LD.
findings.root_cause: The split was meant to strip a ' - <site title>' suffix, which post titles never carry. It cuts legitimate hyphenated titles instead.
findings.proposed_fix: In _includes/article-breadcrumb.html, compute `{% capture bc_suffix %} - {{ site.title }}{% endcapture %}{% assign bc_title = page.title | remove: bc_suffix %}` and use bc_title for both the visible current item and the last JSON-LD ListItem. This is included in the same diff as SD-01 and was verified in the throwaway test build: the full label appears in both places.
findings.rollback: Revert the include change.
findings.benefit: Visible breadcrumb matches the markup and is no longer misleading to readers (e.g. 'Việt' instead of 'Việt - Anh'). Meets the 'markup reflects visible content' policy.
findings.verdict: Không qua phản biện (P3 — workflow chỉ phản biện P0–P2)

findings.title: BlogPosting.image is the site logo (IMG_2536.jpeg, 512x512) on all 6,257 posts, against Google's 'relevant image, not logos' guidance
findings.evidence: values.json: bp.image = 'https://blog.thuexemaynguyentu.com/IMG_2536.jpeg' on 6257/6257 posts. Posts have no own images: 0 front-matter image/cover keys, 0 markdown images, 0 in _posts, and 0 images inside article.post-detail in the build. The logo file is 512x512 JPEG (PIL). The Google Article doc (updated 2026-09-08) says: 'The URL to an image that is representative of the article. Use images that are relevant to the article, rather than logos or captions… Images must represent the marked up content.'
findings.root_cause: _includes/seo.html sets BlogPosting.image to ld_logo whenever a logo exists.
findings.proposed_fix: In _includes/seo.html (BlogPosting block), replace `{% if ld_logo != '' %}"image": {{ ld_logo | jsonify }},{% endif %}` with `{% if page.image %}"image": {{ page.image | absolute_url | jsonify }},{% endif %}`. Article has no required properties, so leaving image out is valid. The logo stays on Organization.logo, LocalBusiness.image and og:image. Verified in the throwaway test build (diff seo.html.diff). Real, article-relevant photos for future posts need owner-supplied images (an editorial decision, outside this fix).
findings.rollback: Revert the 3-line change in seo.html.
findings.benefit: Stops declaring a logo as the representative image of 6,257 articles, as Google's image guidelines require. Lets real images be declared per post later.
findings.verdict: REJECT: (a) The issue is real. The logo is used as BlogPosting.image on all 6,257 posts (FACT, re-measured). The Google Article doc (last updated 2026-09-08, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/article) says: 'Use images that are relevant to the article, rather than logos or
findings.next: Giữ logo làm BlogPosting.image tới khi có ảnh thật; đổi đồng bộ og:image + schema (IMG-05).

findings.title: dateModified is stale on 254 published posts whose content was corrected with revise-published.py; no post shows a visible updated date
findings.evidence: reports/qa-audit/revise/*.json (11 batches) list 254 unique BLG IDs revised (233 on 2026-10-23, 23 on 2026-10-27; 2 revised twice). These are price, legal and deposit corrections. All 254 posts exist in _posts, and 0 have last_modified_at (revised_posts.json). In the build, BlogPosting dateModified == datePublished on 6,253/6,257 posts. The only 4 posts with last_modified_at (2026-10-13) emit a newer dateModified, but post.html shows only page.date. Google publication-dates guidance: 'Make your dates and times consistent… match between the equivalent user-visible and structured values', label dates such as 'Last updated', and dates 'must describe the publication or update date of the page'.
findings.root_cause: revise-published.py may only change body and description, not front matter, so last_modified_at never gets set. seo.html falls back to page.date.
findings.proposed_fix:
(1) Add a deterministic generator, scripts/seo/build-post-modified.py, that writes _data/post-modified.json as {posts: {page.url: {id, modified}}} from reports/qa-audit/revise/*.json (created_at) and the post's article_id/permalink. A working draft is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-blog/c0138ac4-51ee-5beb-a1c9-21d2311d0295/scratchpad/audit/structured-data/build_post_modified.py; its output, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-blog/c0138ac4-51ee-5beb-a1c9-21d2311d0295/scratchpad/audit/structured-data/post-modified.json, covers 254 URLs.
(2) In _includes/seo.html: `{% assign ld_rev = site.data.post-modified.posts[page.url] %}`, then dateModified = ld_rev.modified | default: page.last_modified_at | default: page.date (in the diff). In the throwaway test build, BLG-02110 emitted dateModified 2026-10-23T08:28:10+00:00.
(3) In _layouts/post.html post-meta, show `Cập nhật dd/mm/yyyy` from the same value when it differs from page.date, so the visible and structured dates agree.
(4) Later, in a separate engine PR with tests, have revise-published.py apply refresh the data file.
Do not bump dates for notice-only overlays (legal-notice and price-notice data files) or template changes; that would be artificial freshening.
findings.rollback: Delete _data/post-modified.json, or revert seo.html/post.html; the template falls back to page.date. No change to post bytes, evidence SHA or URLs.
findings.benefit: Accurate update dates for 254 posts with corrected prices and legal facts, which helps Google byline dates and user trust. Visible and structured dates become consistent.
findings.verdict: IMPLEMENT_WITH_CHANGES: (a) The issue is real. Today the structured data says these 254 posts were never modified, but their main content (prices, legal citations, deposit wording) was corrected through the owner-approved revise-published.py process. There are no earlier SEO-master items about dateModified or last_modified

findings.title: LocalBusiness PostalAddress and hours: ward 'Bồ Đề' missing, addressCountry not ISO, hours hard-coded, hasMap/areaServed absent although verified in business.yml
findings.evidence: values.json (7,047 pages): address = {streetAddress '112 Nguyễn Văn Cừ', addressLocality 'Long Biên', addressRegion 'Hà Nội', addressCountry 'Việt Nam'}; hasMap/areaServed/postalCode/geo = null. _data/business.yml has address.district 'Bồ Đề', and the visible footer, /gioi-thieu/, the live main site and the live GBP all show '112 Nguyễn Văn Cừ, Bồ Đề, Long Biên, Hà Nội'. _includes/seo.html hard-codes opens '09:00'/closes '21:00' instead of reading business.hours. business.contact.maps is a visible 'Google Maps' link in the footer; the TinyFish call resolved it to the 'Thuê xe máy ở Hà Nội - Nguyễn Tú' place. business.areas matches the visible 'Khu vực phục vụ' list on /gioi-thieu/. Google LocalBusiness doc example uses addressCountry 'US'; schema.org/addressCountry recommends ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.
findings.root_cause: The template maps only street, city, region and country, and keeps literal hours.
findings.proposed_fix:
In _includes/seo.html (diff provided):
- streetAddress = street + ', ' + business.address.district.
- addressCountry "VN".
- opens/closes parsed from business.hours.
- "hasMap": business.contact.maps.
- "areaServed": business.areas (array of text).
Verified in the throwaway test build: JSON valid; values equal business.yml.
The homepage title, H1, meta and hero are untouched; JSON-LD is not in scripts/seo/frozen-homepage.json.
findings.rollback: Revert the seo.html hunk; values return to the current output.
findings.benefit: LocalBusiness address and hours stay consistent with the visible NAP (name, address, phone) and GBP, and come from one source. No invented data.
findings.verdict: Không qua phản biện (P3 — workflow chỉ phản biện P0–P2)

findings.title: Graph linkage: BlogPosting.author has no url (6,257 posts) and WebSite has no publisher/inLanguage
findings.evidence: values.json: bp.author = {"@type":"Person","name":"Nguyễn Tú"} on 6,257/6,257 posts, with no url or sameAs. The visible byline (span.post-author) is unlinked text and matches the name on all posts (0 mismatches). /gioi-thieu/ opens with 'Giới thiệu Nguyễn Tú' and identifies the person and service. The WebSite node (7,047 pages) has only @id, url, name and description. Google Article doc: author.url is a recommended property, and Google 'can understand both sameAs and url when disambiguating authors'.
findings.root_cause: Minimal BlogPosting.author and WebSite nodes in seo.html.
findings.proposed_fix:
In _includes/seo.html:
- add "url": {{ '/gioi-thieu/' | absolute_url | jsonify }} to BlogPosting.author;
- add "inLanguage": "vi" and "publisher": {"@id": "<site>/#organization"} to WebSite.
Both are in the diff and verified in the throwaway test build. Optionally link the visible byline in _layouts/post.html to /gioi-thieu/ so the markup and visible page agree. Do not add jobTitle, credentials or awards; there is no verified data for them.
findings.rollback: Revert the seo.html lines.
findings.benefit: Clearer author and publisher entities for Google, following the author best practices. No new claims.
findings.verdict: Không qua phản biện (P3 — workflow chỉ phản biện P0–P2)

findings.title: Entity identity is an owner decision: LocalBusiness/Organization url = blog root while GBP website = main site; hard-coded sameAs includes an about.me profile with forbidden claims
findings.evidence:
FACT: Organization.url and LocalBusiness.url = 'https://blog.thuexemaynguyentu.com/' on 7,047 pages. business.yml url and site.business_url = https://thuexemaynguyentu.com/. Live GBP (TinyFish, the maps link) shows 'Thuê xe máy ở Hà Nội - Nguyễn Tú', website thuexemaynguyentu.com, hours 9AM–9PM daily. Main site og:site_name is 'Cho Thuê Xe Máy Hà Nội | Nguyễn Tú', so the brand name differs across the three properties. sameAs is hard-coded in seo.html (4 URLs, duplicated in _data/navigation.yml footer) and omits the main site; the Organization node has no sameAs.
Live: about.me and Pinterest match the business name and phone/address, so they are its own profiles. But the about.me meta description says 'I am a student and web developer in long bien hanoi', and its text claims 'hơn 10 năm kinh nghiệm', which data/business-facts.json forbidden_claims lists as 'số năm kinh nghiệm'. Both profiles list districts (Đống Đa, Cầu Giấy, Hà Đông…) beyond business.yml areas. Facebook (login_required) and TripAdvisor (HTTP 403) are UNKNOWN.
INFERRED: Google's LocalBusiness url is 'the URL of the specific business location' and Organization url 'helps Google uniquely identify your organization', so the blog-root url fragments the entity. The research notes record that the owner treats the main site as a separate property, and the repo forbids cross-site link networks, so this re-opens part of SEO-106 only with owner consent.
findings.root_cause: Original design choice (SEO-106) plus off-site profiles maintained outside the repo.
findings.rollback: Template changes are revertible. Off-site profile edits are owner-controlled.
findings.benefit: Consistent entity signals between the blog, the main site and the GBP. Removes a forbidden claim that the site currently endorses via sameAs and the footer.
findings.next: Chờ chủ website quyết định (xem báo cáo wave4)

findings.title: LocalBusiness postalCode and geo absent: only add from owner-confirmed data
findings.evidence: FACT: postalCode and geo are null on 7,047 pages, and neither exists in _data/business.yml or data/business-facts.json. The live GBP URL contains a pin (21.0409957, 105.8691971). That is scraped, not repo-verified data, so it must not be used without owner confirmation. Google LocalBusiness requires only address and name (both present). geo and postalCode are recommended only. INFERRED/UNKNOWN: Vietnam's 2025 two-tier administrative reform may change the official address format (ward/district). The repo, main site and GBP all currently show '112 Nguyễn Văn Cừ, Bồ Đề, Long Biên, Hà Nội'.
findings.root_cause: No verified postal code or coordinates in the business source files.
findings.proposed_fix: The owner adds address.postal_code, geo.latitude/longitude (from their own GBP pin) and, if needed, the post-reform address to _data/business.yml and data/business-facts.json. seo.html then emits postalCode and GeoCoordinates conditionally (`{% if business.geo %}`). Nothing is added until then.
findings.rollback: Remove the keys from business.yml; the conditional template emits nothing.
findings.benefit: A complete LocalBusiness record without inventing data.
findings.next: Chờ chủ website quyết định (xem báo cáo wave4)

findings.title: Do not 'fix' the +00:00 offsets by setting a timezone in _config.yml: 434 post URLs would shift by one day
findings.evidence: All 6,257 BlogPosting datePublished/dateModified values are valid ISO 8601 with offset +00:00 (the build runs in UTC). They give the same instant as the front matter '+0700'. 0 visible-date mismatches against the structured date, and 0 future dates. 434 posts are dated 00:00–06:59 +0700 (e.g. '2026-09-20 01:10:00 +0700') and have no permalink front matter, so their URL date comes from the build timezone: the built URL is /kinh nghiệm/2026/09/19/ac-quy-xe-tay-ga-yeu-va-khoa-tu/, with visible date 19/09/2026. Adding `timezone: Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` would move those 434 URLs and visible dates to the next day. Google: timezone is recommended, and the date/time must be consistent between visible and structured values, which it currently is.
findings.root_cause: No timezone key in _config.yml; legacy posts without explicit permalinks.
findings.proposed_fix: No change. Keep the current behaviour. Record a guard in docs/SCHEMA-GEO.md or as a CI check: never add `timezone:` to _config.yml while posts without a permalink exist (it would change 434 live URLs, forbidden by AGENTS.md). If +07:00 output is wanted, format only inside JSON-LD without touching page.date. That is optional and low value.
findings.rollback: n/a
findings.benefit: Prevents a well-meant timezone 'fix' from changing 434 live URLs.

findings.title: SEO-106 and schema scope re-checked: keep Organization+LocalBusiness on every page; do not add FAQPage, ItemList/CollectionPage, SearchAction or aggregateRating
findings.evidence:
SEO-106: @graph on 7,047/7,050 pages, 0 parse errors, identical business values everywhere, 0 NAP mismatches against business.yml, business-facts.json and the visible footer. JSON-LD averages 2.6 KB on listings and 4.4 KB on posts (0.9–4.1% of HTML). Google's Organization doc sets no required properties, LocalBusiness needs only address and name (present), and nothing forbids site-wide placement. No new evidence, so it stays DECIDED_KEEP.
FAQPage: 0 emitted; the 2 visible FAQ blocks have schema:false, consistent with docs/SCHEMA-GEO.md and Google's FAQ rich-result restriction.
ItemList/CollectionPage: 0 on 56 topic hubs, 6 hubs and 711 listings. Google's ItemList carousel applies only to Course, Movie, Recipe and Restaurant, so there is no feature to gain.
aggregateRating: the GBP shows 38 reviews averaging 4.1, but Google recommends review/aggregateRating for LocalBusiness 'only for sites that capture reviews about other local businesses' (self-serving), and business-facts.json forbids fabricated reviews.
SearchAction: the sitelinks search box was retired by Google.
findings.root_cause: n/a
findings.proposed_fix: No action. Keep current scope. Re-evaluate SEO-106 only when Search Console data for the blog is connected (SEO-109).
findings.rollback: n/a
findings.benefit: Avoids markup changes that bring no gain or would break policy.

dimensions.summary:
I parsed all 7,050 HTML files in the HEAD a7aaedf build with BeautifulSoup and lxml. The pages break down as 6,257 post, 480 listing, 231 topic-listing, 56 topic, 10 page, 6 hub, 3 category, 3 redirect-stub, 1 each for home, 404, tim-kiem and /chu-de/. Six live URLs fetched through TinyFish return the same title, description, canonical, og and twitter values as the build.

Canonical, robots and H1 are clean. Every page has exactly one H1. There are no duplicate titles, no empty headings, and canonical always equals og:url. Only 404 and tim-kiem carry noindex, and neither is in the sitemap. The 3 redirect stubs point their canonical at the target and use a 0s meta refresh.

The main new issue is the title suffix. _includes/seo.html adds " - Thuê Xe Máy Hà Nội Nguyễn Tú" to 7,039 titles, and 7 hub or /chu-de/ titles hard-code " - Cẩm nang Thuê Xe Máy Hà Nội Nguyễn Tú". As a result the commercial head term appears in 7,044 of 7,045 indexable titles, and 18 titles contain it twice. This contradicts the documented K01 rule that the blog should not compete for this term, and it goes against Google's title-link guidance on boilerplate and concise branding. 89.6% of titles are over 60 characters and 83% are over 70.

The fix is template-only and keeps the frozen homepage unchanged. I tested the Liquid with the liquid 4.0.4 gem. It strips the long suffixes and appends " | " + business.brand, which matches the homepage's "| Nguyễn Tú". The head term would then appear in only the 18 titles whose own text contains it, never twice, with 0 duplicate titles. No checker asserts the long suffix: check-regressions.py checks only the homepage title, which this fix does not change.

Other findings:
- **Long titles in new content:** post titles themselves are getting longer, with a median of 45 characters in September, 85 in early October and 100 in late October. Every one of the 46 newest refill candidates is 104 or more characters.
- **og/twitter cards:** every page shares one 512x512 logo but declares a summary_large_image card. No post has an image.
- **hreflang:** self-only vi and x-default links appear on 7,047 pages of a single-language site, including the 404 and tim-kiem pages.
- **Topic hub descriptions:** 51 of 56 are under 70 characters.
- **Headings:** 8 static pages skip from h2 to h4. /bao-mat/ and /dieu-khoan/ get bogus h2s from a broken markdown list. A head-term CTA h3 sits under "Bài viết liên quan" on 6,319 pages.
- **Site name:** the homepage title uses "Nguyễn Tú", but WebSite.name and og:site_name use "Thuê Xe Máy Hà Nội Nguyễn Tú".

Outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-blog/c0138ac4-51ee-5beb-a1c9-21d2311d0295/scratchpad/audit/head-meta/: audit_head_meta.py, analyze.py, summary.json, rows.json, head-meta-pages.csv, simulate_suffix.py, title-suffix-simulation.csv, seo_title_proposed.liquid and test_liquid.rb.

findings.title: Site-wide title suffix puts the commercial head term 'thuê xe máy Hà Nội' into 7,044 of 7,045 indexable titles; replace it with a short brand suffix in seo.html
findings.evidence:
Source: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-blog/c0138ac4-51ee-5beb-a1c9-21d2311d0295/scratchpad/audit/head-meta/analyze.py over 7,050 build files, saved to summary.json.

What the build shows:
- _includes/seo.html lines 3-12 append ' - ' + site.title (' - Thuê Xe Máy Hà Nội Nguyễn Tú', 31 characters) whenever page.title does not already contain site.title. The result is 7,039 titles with that suffix.
- 7 titles hard-code ' - Cẩm nang Thuê Xe Máy Hà Nội Nguyễn Tú': thue-xe.md, xe-may.md, an-toan-phap-ly.md, cung-duong.md, ky-nang.md, hoi-dap.md and chu-de.md. The template skips its own suffix for these.
- scripts/factory/generate-listing-pages.py lines 92 and 120 hard-code the long suffix into 711 generated listing/topic-listing titles.
- The head term appears in 7,044 of 7,045 indexable titles. Only 24 titles would contain it without the suffix.
- 18 titles contain it twice: 11 /thue-xe/* topics ('Đặt cọc & giữ giấy tờ - Thuê xe máy Hà Nội - Thuê Xe Máy Hà Nội Nguyễn Tú'), the /thue-xe/ hub, /bang-gia/ and 5 posts.
- Lengths: 89.6% of indexable titles exceed 60 characters and 83.0% exceed 70; for posts the figures are 99.3% and 93.2%.

Why it matters:
- scripts/seo/seo-matrix-config.yml K01 records main_site_conflict CAO with the mitigation 'Không tạo thêm trang nhắm head term này', and the lead URL for the head term is the frozen homepage.
- The research file keyword-serp-2026-10-31.json now describes the main site as an independent competitor. Sitewide keyword boilerplate is still not a method Google recommends for either strategy.
- Live fetch through TinyFish shows the same titles on /, /thue-xe/, /thue-xe/dat-coc/, /bang-gia/, /an-toan-phap-ly/bao-hiem/trang/2/ and the blog's only top-10 URL (#4 for 'thuê xe máy phố cổ hà nội'), which has a 103-character title.

Checks that touch titles:
- scripts/seo/check-regressions.py H1 compares only the homepage title against frozen-homepage.json; H8 checks for bare ampersands.
- test_live_url_audit.py uses synthetic pages.
- scripts/seo/build-inventory.py title_in_html_ok is a post-level reporting field and is a substring check.
- No test or checker asserts the long suffix.

Simulation and test:
- Proposed template (simulate_suffix.py, written to title-suffix-simulation.csv): head term in 18 titles, never twice, 0 duplicate titles. Indexable titles over 60 characters fall from 6,311 to 5,081, posts over 70 from 5,830 to 4,394, and the median length from 106 to 87.
- The Liquid was tested with the liquid 4.0.4 gem (test_liquid.rb). The homepage stays 'Thuê xe máy 50cc–125cc tại Hà Nội | Nguyễn Tú', /thue-xe/ becomes 'Thuê xe máy Hà Nội | Nguyễn Tú', and listing pages become 'Chia sẻ - Trang 2 | Nguyễn Tú'.
findings.root_cause: seo.html uses site.title, which is a keyword plus brand string, as the per-page title suffix. Hubs and the listing generator also hard-code a longer variant. The documented brand used on the frozen homepage is 'Nguyễn Tú' (business.brand in _data/business.yml).
findings.rollback: git revert the single seo.html commit; the next Pages deploy restores the previous titles. Nothing else depends on the new suffix.
findings.benefit:
Inferred benefits:
- Titles become distinct and concise, as Google recommends, and the brand matches the frozen homepage.
- Removes 7,026 instances of head-term boilerplate, bringing the template in line with the K01 non-cannibalization strategy.
- Lowers the chance that Google rewrites titles or truncates the suffix on mobile.
- Saves about 0.5 MB of HTML across the title, og:title and twitter:title tags.

No URL, canonical or post-source change is involved.
findings.verdict: IMPLEMENT_WITH_CHANGES: (a) The issue is real. I re-measured it on site-base and the auditor's counts are correct. Source: _includes/seo.html lines 4-13 append ' - ' + site.title. In addition, 14 static .md titles and scripts/factory/generate-listing-pages.py (lines 92 and 120) hard-code the long suffix. Result: the commer

findings.title: Post titles are getting much longer: median base title (without suffix) grew from 45 to 100 characters, and every one of the 46 newest refill candidates is 104 or more characters
findings.evidence:
Base title lengths of posts, with the suffix removed (rows.json):

| Publish window | Posts | Median length | Over 70 chars |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-16 to 09-30 | 963 | 45 | 55 |
| 2026-10-01 to 10-15 | 4,542 | 85 | 3,026 |
| 2026-10-16 to 10-31 | 699 | 100 | 699 |

Overall, 4,305 of 6,257 posts (68.8%) are over 60 characters, 3,138 are over 80, and the longest is 131 ('Va chạm xe máy chỉ hư hỏng nhẹ, không ai bị thương: đơn yêu cầu giải quyết, thỏa thuận dân sự tại chỗ và thông báo kết quả của CSGT').

The pipeline is still producing long titles. The latest batches, data/factory/refill-batches/refill-2026-10-30-R30A/B/C.json, hold 46 candidates with min 104, median about 113 and max 120 characters; all 46 are over 70.

docs/QUALITY-RUBRIC.md line 21 scores the title as 'Title đúng intent ... ≤ 60 ký tự hiển thị hợp lý' (20 points). However, scripts/factory/factory-operator.py s_crit 'title_match' only checks equality with the matrix title and never checks length, so the rubric limit is not enforced.

slugkit.py builds the slug as slugify(title)[:MAX_SLUG_LEN], so long titles also produce slugs cut mid-word, for example '...canh-gio-nhan-de-kip-d'. The title also becomes the H1 and the BlogPosting headline.
findings.root_cause: Refill and coordinator topic generation writes full question-plus-explainer sentences as titles. The QA scorer has no length check, even though the rubric documents one.
findings.proposed_fix:
Published posts: do not touch them (BLOCKED_RULE; this would need revise-published.py with owner approval, and slugs and permalinks are immutable).

For PLANNED and future rows, the owner should decide on three changes:
(a) Add an advisory gate in stage-refill-batch / gates G1–G9 or the writer `check`: warn when a title is over about 70 characters and refuse when it is over about 90. This needs owner approval because it changes refill gates.
(b) Ask coordinators to write titles as a short primary query plus a brief qualifier (aim for 50–65 characters), with the long explanation moved into the description and the H2s.
(c) Before materialization, shorten the 46 STAGED candidates in R30A/B/C. Nothing is published from them yet, so their URLs are not live.

Do not lower QA thresholds.
findings.rollback: Gate and guideline changes are config or docs changes that can be reverted with git revert. Rows that have not been published can be retitled freely before materialization.
findings.benefit: Inferred: shorter title links and less truncation or rewriting for every future post. It also gives shorter and cleaner slugs and a better match with the rubric's own 60-character guidance.
findings.next: Chờ chủ website quyết định (xem báo cáo wave4)

findings.title: Static pages, categories and hubs need descriptive seo_title overrides once the long suffix is removed (about 20 titles drop to 30 characters or fewer, for example 'Blog | Nguyễn Tú')
findings.evidence:
title-suffix-simulation.csv shows that after HM-01 these titles become very short:
- /bai-viet/ → 'Blog | Nguyễn Tú' (16 characters)
- /chia-se/, /du-lich/ and /lien-he/ → 19 characters each
- /gioi-thieu/ → 22
- /kinh-nghiem/ → 23
- /chu-de/ → 'Tất cả chủ đề | Nguyễn Tú' (25)
- /bang-gia-xe-ga/ and /bang-gia-xe-so/ → 26
- /xe-may/ → 'Xe máy & dòng xe | Nguyễn Tú' (28)
- /an-toan-phap-ly/ → 29
- /bao-mat/ and /dieu-khoan/ → 30

Google advises against vague title descriptors such as 'Home' or 'Profile'. Paginated listing titles such as 'Du lịch - Trang 12 | Nguyễn Tú' are fine because Google allows the same titles across a pagination series.
findings.root_cause: Today these short page names only read as descriptive because the keyword-style suffix is attached. Their front-matter titles double as the H1 source through split ' - ', so the visible title can't be lengthened without also changing the H1.
findings.proposed_fix:
HM-01 adds support for page.seo_title. Use it to add a `seo_title:` line to the front matter of the static pages, categories and hubs (not _posts), with descriptive titles containing no new business data. Suggested values:
- blog.md: 'Tất cả bài viết cẩm nang xe máy'
- lien-he.md: 'Liên hệ thuê xe máy Nguyễn Tú'
- gioi-thieu.md: 'Giới thiệu dịch vụ cho thuê xe máy'
- kinh-nghiem.md: 'Kinh nghiệm thuê và đi xe máy'
- chia-se.md: 'Chia sẻ kinh nghiệm đi xe máy'
- du-lich.md: 'Du lịch Hà Nội bằng xe máy'
- chu-de.md: 'Tất cả chủ đề cẩm nang xe máy'
- bang-gia-xe-ga.md: 'Bảng giá thuê xe tay ga'
- bang-gia-xe-so.md: 'Bảng giá thuê xe số'
- the remaining bang-gia-*, hubs, bao-mat and dieu-khoan along the same lines

The template then appends ' | Nguyễn Tú'. title, H1, permalink and canonical stay unchanged. Ship this in the same PR as HM-01.
findings.rollback: Delete the seo_title lines (git revert); the template then falls back to page.title.
findings.benefit: Inferred: descriptive and distinct titles on navigation and commercial-support pages, such as the K04 lead /bang-gia/ and the supporting pages, without bringing back sitewide head-term boilerplate.
findings.verdict: Không qua phản biện (P3 — workflow chỉ phản biện P0–P2)

findings.title: Every page uses a twitter:card of summary_large_image with a 512x512 square logo as its only image; no post has its own image
findings.evidence: summary.json counts: - og:image is https://blog.thuexemaynguyentu.com/IMG_2536.jpeg on 7,047 pages. It declares 512x512 and image/jpeg, and PIL confirms the file is (512, 512) JPEG. - twitter:card is summary_large_image on 7,047 pages. - 0 of 6,257 _posts have an image: front-matter key or or ![]() in the body. - og:locale is absent, so Facebook defaults to en_US, while html lang is vi. - og:image:alt is absent. - No page sets max-image-preview. The live fetch shows the same tags.
findings.root_cause: seo.html hard-codes summary_large_image and uses business.logo for every page.
findings.proposed_fix:
SAFE_TEMPLATE changes in _includes/seo.html:
(1) Emit `<meta name="twitter:card" content="{% if page.image %}summary_large_image{% else %}summary{% endif %}">`. Summary cards suit a square image of at least 144x144.
(2) Add `<meta property="og:locale" content="vi_VN">`.
(3) Add `<meta property="og:image:alt" content="{{ business.brand }}">`.
(4) Prepare an optional page.image branch, using that image for og:image and twitter:image, for when real photos exist.

Adding real photos of at least 1200px, plus `max-image-preview:large`, so that pages can appear with large Discover and Search previews is a NEEDS_OWNER content and asset decision. Do not generate fake photos.
findings.rollback: Revert the seo.html change.
findings.benefit: Inferred: link previews on X and other platforms stop cropping the logo into a 2:1 frame and display correctly, and Facebook previews are labelled with the right locale. Discover eligibility would need real large images (owner decision).
findings.verdict: Không qua phản biện (P3 — workflow chỉ phản biện P0–P2)

findings.title: Self-only hreflang (vi plus x-default pointing to the same URL) is emitted on 7,047 pages of a single-language site, including the 404 and noindex tim-kiem pages
findings.evidence:
From summary.json:
- 7,047 pages carry the hreflang set vi + x-default; only the 3 redirect stubs have none.
- Both href values always equal the page's own canonical (0 mismatches).
- The set is also present on /404.html (canonical https://blog.thuexemaynguyentu.com/404.html) and /tim-kiem/ (noindex).
- Together the tags add about 2.31 MB of HTML across the build, roughly 328 bytes per page.

The site is Vietnamese only: _config.yml excludes en/, so no alternate-language versions exist.

scripts/seo/build-master-xlsx.py writes the HREFLANG MATRIX decision as 'Không ghép cặp ngôn ngữ ... Không tạo hreflang giả' (no language pairing, no fake hreflang). The template contradicts that documented decision.

Per Google, hreflang is for pages with multiple language or region versions, and 'Google doesn't use hreflang or the HTML lang attribute to detect the language of a page'. A self-only set is valid syntax and not harmful, but it provides no benefit.
findings.root_cause: The block in _includes/seo.html labelled '<!-- Hreflang for Vietnamese only -->' is left over from an earlier bilingual setup.
findings.proposed_fix:
Remove the two `<link rel="alternate" hreflang=...>` lines from _includes/seo.html. If an English edition ever ships, reintroduce them behind a condition that requires a real alternate URL, for example `{% if page.translations %}`.

Best shipped in the same deploy as HM-01 so all pages change only once.
findings.rollback: Revert the seo.html change.
findings.benefit: Removes dead markup (about 2.3 MB of HTML) and the contradiction with the documented hreflang decision, and stops alternate links pointing at /404.html. Expected ranking effect is neutral (inferred).
findings.verdict: Không qua phản biện (P3 — workflow chỉ phản biện P0–P2)

findings.title: Topic hub meta descriptions are too short: 51 of 56 are under 70 characters (minimum 37), and these hubs are the lead URLs for K02, K03 and K06–K10
findings.evidence:
summary.json desc_len_by_tpl for topic pages: median 56.5, minimum 37, maximum 114; 51 of 56 are under 70 characters. Examples:
- /du-lich/ho-tay/: 'Khu Hồ Tây, đền thờ và ven sông Hồng.' (37)
- /cung-duong/moc-chau/ (43)
- /du-lich/pho-co/ (44)
- /thue-xe/dat-coc/: 'Tiền đặt cọc, hình thức giữ giấy tờ, hoàn cọc khi trả xe.' (57; confirmed live)

By contrast, hubs have medians of 98–129 characters and posts 83–200 with 0 duplicates.

The topic .md files are hand-maintained. generate-topic-hubs.py only creates missing hubs and has hub intros of 60 words or more (SEO-007), so the source text for longer descriptions already exists.

The topic layout also shows page.description as visible text (p.page-description).

Out of scope here (NO_ACTION):
- The 231 topic-listing pages use the site default description.
- The 480 listing pages use thin descriptions like 'Các bài viết Chia sẻ, trang 2/10.'.

Google's pagination guidance allows the same titles and descriptions across a series.
findings.root_cause: Topic front-matter descriptions were seeded from short data/content-taxonomy.json child descriptions and never expanded.
findings.proposed_fix:
Rewrite the description: field in the 51 topic .md files (thue-xe/*.md, xe-may/*.md, an-toan-phap-ly/*.md, cung-duong/*.md, ky-nang/*.md, hoi-dap/*.md, du-lich/*.md) to 110–160 characters. Summarize each hub's existing intro text. Rules for the rewrite: - No prices, deposits, fees or other new facts. - No repeated head-term phrasing. - Keep each description unique. Do not change title, permalink or the intro body. Re-run validate-hub-intros.py and check-regressions H5/H6 afterwards. intro_words counts text between and the first

, so a longer description only increases it.
findings.rollback: git revert the .md description edits.
findings.benefit: Inferred: better snippet candidates on the hub URLs that the keyword map designates as leads, such as /thue-xe/thue-thang/, /thue-xe/thue-theo-dia-diem/ and /du-lich/long-bien/. Google mostly builds snippets from page content, so the expected lift is modest.
findings.verdict: Không qua phản biện (P3 — workflow chỉ phản biện P0–P2)

findings.title: Heading-structure defects on static pages: FAQ questions skip from h2 to h4 on 8 pages, and a broken contact list creates bogus h2s and an empty <li> on /bao-mat/ and /dieu-khoan/
findings.evidence:
h2→h4 skips (analyze.py heading_skips): 8 pages — /bai-viet/, /bang-gia/, /bang-gia-xe-50cc/, /bang-gia-xe-dien/, /bang-gia-xe-ga/, /bang-gia-xe-so/, /gioi-thieu/ and /kinh-nghiem/. In each, '## Câu hỏi thường gặp' is followed directly by '#### question' lines, for example bang-gia.md lines 116–132, blog.md lines 85–101 and kinh-nghiem.md lines 130–138. Broken contact list: in bao-mat.md lines 62–64 and dieu-khoan.md lines 89–91, `- {% include icon.html ... %} **Điện thoại:** ...` places a multi-line SVG inside a markdown list item. kramdown then renders: - an empty
  • -

    Điện thoại: …

    -

    Zalo: …

    That is 2 bogus h2s per page, confirmed with grep on the build. The two pages also repeat the H1 text as their first h2 ('Chính sack bảo mật' and 'Điều khoản sử dụng'). No empty headings exist anywhere, and there is exactly 1 H1 on all 7,050 pages.

findings.proposed_fix:
SAFE_PAGE_CONTENT edits, all outside _posts: (1) In bang-gia.md, bang-gia-xe-50cc.md, bang-gia-xe-dien.md, bang-gia-xe-ga.md, bang-gia-xe-so.md, gioi-thieu.md, blog.md and kinh-nghiem.md, change the FAQ '####' lines to '###'. Check CSS for any h4-specific FAQ styling first. (2) In bao-mat.md lines 62–64 and dieu-khoan.md lines 89–91, drop the `{% include icon.html %}` calls from the markdown list items. Alternatively, render those 3 lines as an HTML
    with the icons. The phone, Zalo and email values still come from business.yml variables, so no business data changes. Optionally remove the duplicate '## Chính sách bảo mật' and '## Điều khoản sử dụng' first h2s. Verify with analyze.py: heading_skips should be 0 and no `
  • ` should remain.

findings.title: Site-name signals disagree: the frozen homepage title uses the brand 'Nguyễn Tú', but WebSite.name and og:site_name on every page use the keyword-style 'Thuê Xe Máy Hà Nội Nguyễn Tú'
findings.evidence:
- The homepage <title> is 'Thuê xe máy 50cc–125cc tại Hà Nội | Nguyễn Tú' (frozen).
- og:site_name and JSON-LD WebSite.name are site.title, 'Thuê Xe Máy Hà Nội Nguyễn Tú', on 7,047 pages (seo.html; confirmed live on /).
- _data/business.yml has brand: 'Nguyễn Tú' and display_name: 'Thuê Xe Máy Hà Nội Nguyễn Tú'.

Google supports site names at subdomain level, so blog.thuexemaynguyentu.com gets its own site name. The site-names guidance says WebSite structured data matters most, that the name should be concise and not generic, and that it should be used consistently across the home page.

This finding overlaps with the structured-data dimension. It is listed here because og:site_name is a head tag.
findings.root_cause: site.title doubles as both the SEO keyword string and the brand name.
findings.proposed_fix:
This is an owner decision on the official site name for the blog subdomain.

Recommended option: set WebSite.name and og:site_name to business.brand ('Nguyễn Tú') or another owner-chosen concise name. Add WebSite.alternateName ['Thuê Xe Máy Hà Nội Nguyễn Tú', 'blog.thuexemaynguyentu.com'].

Only _includes/seo.html would change. The frozen homepage title, H1, meta description and hero would not, and title links are unaffected by this change.
findings.rollback: Revert the seo.html change.
findings.benefit: Inferred: a more consistent site-name signal and a better chance that Google shows the brand rather than a generic phrase as the site name.
findings.next: Chờ chủ website quyết định (xem báo cáo wave4)

findings.title: Already correct, no action needed: canonical, og:url, robots, H1 count, title uniqueness and redirect stubs all pass on all 7,050 pages
findings.evidence:
From summary.json:
- Canonical: 0 pages missing it and 0 with more than one. Every non-stub canonical is self-referencing; the 483 legacy paths with spaces or diacritics are percent-encoded but resolve to themselves. canonical equals og:url on every page (0 mismatches).
- Titles: 0 duplicate groups, and exactly one <title> on every page.
- H1: exactly one on all 7,050 pages, and each post's H1 matches its title without the suffix.
- Headings: 0 empty headings.
- Robots: noindex only on /404.html and /tim-kiem/ (both 'noindex,follow' and excluded from the sitemap; check-regressions H7b PASS).
- Redirect stubs (3): canonical points to the target, 0s meta refresh, sitemap: false.
- Meta descriptions: present on every page except the 3 stubs, and 0 duplicates among indexable non-paginated pages.
- <meta name="title"> appears only on the homepage. It is non-standard and ignored by Google, and the homepage is frozen.
- 227 post descriptions over 160 characters (maximum 200) are acceptable, since Google sets no length limit.

The live fetch of 6 URLs matched the build.
findings.proposed_fix: No change. Keep check-regressions.py H2, H7b and H8 as the guard. After HM-01, add one invariant for title boilerplate (see HM-01 Phase 2).
findings.benefit: Prevents re-auditing items that are already correct.

dimensions.dimension: internal links & site architecture (Homepage > Pillar > Hub > Silo > Supporting articles)
dimensions.summary:
I built a link graph from the existing local build of HEAD a7aaedfc (7,050 HTML files, 653,639 internal anchors, URLs normalised and percent-decoded). Scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-blog/c0138ac4-51ee-5beb-a1c9-21d2311d0295/scratchpad/audit/internal-links/ (build_graph.py, analyze.py, out/*.json|tsv, group-map-12.csv, invalid-taxonomy-posts.csv, metrics.json). Two live checks via TinyFish confirmed the main defects.

Overall the architecture is healthy and flat. Every page in the sitemap can be reached from "/". The deepest pages are at 5 clicks, and those are only 45 pages of the old category pagination. Posts sit 1–4 clicks from the homepage (99.9% at 3 or fewer). All 56 hubs and 7 pillars are 1 click from the homepage. The 231 hub pagination pages are 2 clicks away, and no hub paginates beyond 9 pages. No post has zero inbound links: 6,197 posts get exactly 4 "Bài viết liên quan" links each. The 181 posts added since the 2026-10-23 inventory are all linked from page 1 of their hub, and each links to its own hub.

New problems found:
(1) The /du-lich/ pillar still uses the old category layout. Live, it lists only 4 of its 6 hubs, with wrong post counts (11/3/2/1 instead of 196/97/93/113). It omits Bảo tàng (95 posts) and Long Biên (102). Its breadcrumb also differs from the other pillars.
(2) 14 PUBLISHED posts have parent_id/child_id values in front matter that do not exist in the taxonomy, although the matrix holds the correct values. Ten of them appear on no hub page; if related, prev/next and body links are ignored, these 10 cannot be reached at all. Four of them output an invalid BreadcrumbList (name:null, item "//"). The cause is that no gate checks front-matter taxonomy against the taxonomy and the matrix.
(3) The commercial price pages are disconnected from the topic hubs. /bang-gia/, /bang-gia-xe-so/ and /gioi-thieu/ point the anchor "kinh nghiệm thuê xe máy tại Hà Nội" at the old chronological list /kinh-nghiem/ (4,712 posts over 393 pages). Six model or electric hubs do not link to their price page.
(4) Hubs with the same intent in different pillars mostly do not link to each other.

Effects measured on the build:
- All 14 breadcrumbs lack the hub link; 4 also lack the pillar link.
- In article-breadcrumb.html the JSON-LD still emits position 3 with name:null, item 'https://blog.thuexemaynguyentu.com//', and position 4 with item:null. The visible trail has 3 items, the JSON-LD 5.
- 10 posts (the C-HD/C-THUE typos and the 'undefined' ones) appear on no hub or hub-pagination page. Their only listing links come from /kinh-nghiem/trang/62..359/ and /du-lich/trang/19/.

- BLG-01591 gets 0 'related' inbound links and BLG-00513 gets 1 (site norm is 4).
Live check (TinyFish) confirmed: the BLG-01382 trail is 'Trang chủ › Cẩm nang › <title>', and the BLG-03652 and BLG-01591 trails have no hub. Full list: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-blog/c0138ac4-51ee-5beb-a1c9-21d2311d0295/scratchpad/audit/internal-links/invalid-taxonomy-posts.csv.
findings.root_cause: Writer drafts were published with wrong taxonomy IDs in front matter. The templates and the listing generator trust front matter, and nothing checks it against the taxonomy or matrix (see IL-03). The front matter cannot be edited because content_sha256 evidence binds the file.
findings.proposed_fix:
Correct this at render time only; no _posts edit and no URL change.
1) Add _data/taxonomy-overrides.yml (non-business, generated from data/content-matrix.csv truth), keyed by article_id with {p, c} for exactly these 14 IDs, e.g. `BLG-01382: {p: P-PHAP-LY, c: C-BAO-HIEM}`.
2) In _includes/article-breadcrumb.html, after the factory-map fallback, add `{% assign bc_ov = site.data.taxonomy-overrides[page.article_id] %}{% if bc_ov %}{% assign bc_parent_id = bc_ov.p %}{% assign bc_child_id = bc_ov.c %}{% endif %}`.
3) Add the same override block in _layouts/post.html where art_parent_id/art_child_id are set, so related-articles uses the right cluster or parent fallback.
4) Harden the JSON-LD in article-breadcrumb.html: emit the parent item only `{% if bc_parent %}` and the child item only `{% if bc_parent and bc_child_node %}`, computing position numbers so they mirror the visible trail. Then it can never emit null or '//' again.
Hub listing inclusion needs the generator change in IL-03. Verify: rebuild, then check the 14 URLs show 'Trang chủ › Cẩm nang › Pillar › Hub › Bài' with 5 valid ListItems; grep the build for '"name": null' in BreadcrumbList (expect 0); run check-regressions 9/9 and check-built-links.

findings.title: Root cause: no gate checks a draft's front-matter parent_id/child_id against the taxonomy and matrix row; listing generator trusts front matter
findings.evidence: `grep -n 'parent_id|child_id' scripts/factory/qa.py scripts/factory/publish-gate.py` returns nothing. scripts/factory/validate.py (L346-352) validates matrix rows only (`r['parent_id'] not in pmap or r['child_id'] not in cmap`), not post front matter. scripts/factory/generate-listing-pages.py L63-69 reads child_id straight from post front matter, so an invalid value excludes the post from every hub listing. Result: 14 PUBLISHED posts with invalid IDs (IL-02), the earliest from 2026-09-27 and the latest from 2026-10-15. Each future occurrence silently removes a post from the hub silo.
findings.root_cause: The factory checks taxonomy at the matrix level, while the rendered site uses front matter. There is no consistency check between the two.
findings.proposed_fix:
Factory engine change; needs owner approval and engine tests:
(1) Add a check in validate.py --scope chunk and in writer-session.py `check`: refuse a draft whose parent_id/child_id is missing from data/content-taxonomy.json, whose child belongs to another parent, or whose IDs differ from its matrix row. This adds a correctness check; it does not lower any QA threshold.
(2) In generate-listing-pages.py, when a post's front-matter child_id is invalid, fall back to the matrix child_id (or to _data/taxonomy-overrides.yml from IL-02), so the 10 posts are listed in their hubs.
(3) Add a regression test (e.g. scripts/factory/tests/test_frontmatter_taxonomy.py) seeded with the 'undefined' and P-AN-TOAN-PHAP-LY cases.
findings.rollback: Revert the engine commit; the check only refuses new drafts and does not mutate published state.
findings.benefit: Stops future posts being published outside the hub structure, and gets the 10 existing posts listed on their hub pages.
findings.next: Chờ chủ website quyết định (xem báo cáo wave4)

dimensions.dimension: performance (Core Web Vitals lab) + accessibility + mobile UX of main templates
dimensions.summary:
LAB-ONLY audit of build a7aaedfc (8 URLs: /, /thue-xe/, /thue-xe/thue-thang/, /bang-gia/, /kinh-nghiem/, /kinh-nghiem/trang/2/, newest post /cung-duong/2026/10/31/tu-bac-ha-sang-xin-man-...-ha-giang/, legacy post /du lịch/2026/09/19/thue-xe-may-quan-hoan-kiem-gan-pho-co/). Tools: Lighthouse 12.8.2 (mobile default and --preset=desktop), axe-core through Playwright at 390x844 (light and dark), keyboard probes, screenshots. These are not CrUX field data. GitHub Pages CDN was not measured, and GSC is not connected.

Important caveat: python http.server sends no gzip, which inflates mobile numbers. A second server (node, gzip, Cache-Control max-age=600, mimicking GitHub Pages) gives the more representative lab results.
- On the gzip server every non-home page scores 100 on mobile: FCP about 1.20 s, LCP 1.22-1.66 s, CLS about 0, TBT about 0.
- The homepage is the only weak page: perf 95-97, LCP 2.48-2.87 s (just over the 2.5 s "good" threshold). It ships 424 KB, mostly 1200x800 JPEGs of 100-132 KB with no srcset.
- Every page has 4-5 separate unminified render-blocking stylesheets (81-84 KB raw, about 13.8 KB gz). Lighthouse estimates 340-390 ms of FCP savings.

A prototype in a scratchpad overlay (repo untouched) used responsive WebP, a 96 px logo, one CSS bundle, and deferred scripts with the business/assistant data in a deferred file:
- Home: LCP 2.48-2.87 s became 1.66-1.71 s, FCP 1.21-1.26 s became 0.91-0.96 s, bytes went from 424 KB to 145 KB.
- Hub and post: FCP about 1.20 s became about 0.90 s.
- It stayed functionally identical: assistant answers and calculator WhatsApp link unchanged, 0 JS errors, and full-page heights identical at 390 and 1280 px.

Accessibility (Lighthouse a11y 90-96, SEO 100 and Best Practices 100 on all 16 runs):
- color-contrast fails on all 8 templates: footer copyright in light mode, plus dark-mode article links, .btn-primary and footer. 57 nodes.
- link-in-text-block (WCAG 1.4.1) on hub/page prose: 56 nodes.
- The assistant toggle has a label-in-name mismatch on every page, and its modal does not trap or return focus.
- The floating-widget focus protection is broken because scroll-padding is set on body instead of html.
- 8 static pages skip from h2 to h4.
A candidate CSS file validated by injection removes all 113 contrast and link nodes, and the html scroll-padding fix removes the one fully-obscured focus stop found.

Inline window.NGUYEN_TU_* data: 8,486 B raw (2,642 B gz) on 7,047 of 7,050 HTML files, about 59.8 MB raw across the build. NGUYEN_TU_PRICING (3,703 B) is read only by calculator.js, which loads on 2 pages.

Blank lines from Liquid loops make up 106.7 MB of the 804 MB of HTML. The 711 /trang/ listing pages go from 367 KB to 86 KB raw (−22% gz) without them.

None of the proposed fixes touch _posts, URLs, canonicals, business data, or frozen homepage text. No overlap with SEO-001..121; theme PRs #28-#30 never measured CWV or contrast. All local servers were stopped.

Artifacts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-blog/c0138ac4-51ee-5beb-a1c9-21d2311d0295/scratchpad/audit/performance-a11y/:
- lh/, lhgz/, lhproto/: Lighthouse JSON
- metrics-summary.json, lh-summary.json
- axe/axe-results.json
- candidate-fix.css
- overlay/: prototype
- shots/: screenshots (*-390-viewport.png, *-390-full.png, proto-*.png, diff-*.png)

findings.title: Homepage ships 1200x800 JPEGs (100-132 KB each) with no responsive or modern-format variants. Lab mobile LCP is 2.5-2.9 s.
findings.evidence:
Lighthouse mobile on the gzip server, 3 runs of /:
- Perf 95-97. LCP 2,481 / 2,760 / 2,865 ms; Lighthouse labels LCP 'needs improvement' above 2,500 ms. On python http.server LCP is 4,057 ms.
- Total weight 423,827 B, of which about 552 KB raw is vehicle photos.
- image-delivery-insight: 'Est savings of 324 KiB', LCP savings 600 ms.
- Examples: xe-so-honda-wave.jpeg (132,405 B) is used as the hero with fetchpriority=high, intrinsic 1200x800 but displayed 425x284. xe-50cc.jpeg and xe-tay-ga-honda-vision.jpeg are displayed 378x252.
- On mobile the LCP element is p.hero-subtitle, with 84% render delay. The 132 KB high-priority hero and lazy service images (fetched early, inside Chrome's lazy-load distance) compete with CSS for bandwidth.
- On desktop the LCP element is the hero img (845 ms).

Prototype in overlay/ (WebP 480w/800w with srcset/sizes; files measured hero 16,454 / 33,000 B, other cars 9-29 KB): LCP 1,658-1,710 ms, perf 99-100, bytes 144,633. Pixel diff shows only photo re-encoding, with identical page height.

The 5 image paths come from _data/business.yml lines 29-51. They are used only in _layouts/home.html (lines 33 and 88), not in seo.html schema.
findings.root_cause: _layouts/home.html renders vehicle.image directly (single JPEG src, no srcset/sizes). No image pipeline exists in the static build.
findings.proposed_fix:
SAFE_TEMPLATE. Do not edit _data/business.yml.
1. Add pre-generated WebP variants next to each JPEG, for example assets/images/services/xe-so-honda-wave-480.webp and -800.webp. Generate them once with PIL at quality ~78 and commit the binaries.
2. In _layouts/home.html, derive the variant paths in Liquid:
   `{% assign v480 = vehicle.image | replace: '.jpeg', '-480.webp' %}`
   `{% assign v800 = vehicle.image | replace: '.jpeg', '-800.webp' %}`
   Emit srcset only if both exist (`site.static_files | where: 'path', v480 | first`), otherwise fall back to the current JPEG.
3. Emit `src="{{ v800 }}" srcset="{{ v480 }} 480w, {{ v800 }} 800w"`.
   - Hero (line 33): `sizes="(max-width: 767px) calc(100vw - 32px), 640px"`. Keep fetchpriority=high, since the hero is the desktop LCP. Keep the width/height attributes.
   - Service cards (lines 87-92): `sizes="(max-width: 767px) calc(100vw - 32px), 400px"`. Keep loading=lazy.
4. Leave H1, title, meta and hero_description untouched; check-regressions.py compares frozen text only.

Verify: rerun Lighthouse mobile on /, check-built-links, check-regressions.py 9/9.

Expected impact (lab, measured in prototype): home LCP about -0.8 to -1.2 s, -279 KB per first visit.
findings.rollback: git revert of the home.html commit restores the single-JPEG markup. The extra .webp files are inert and can stay or be removed.
findings.benefit: Homepage (the main commercial landing page) moves from 'needs improvement' to 'good' lab LCP on mobile. It also uses about 66% fewer bytes on mobile data.
findings.verdict:
IMPLEMENT_WITH_CHANGES: (a) The problem is real, but parts of the claim are overstated.
- FACT: the homepage serves 552 KB of 1200–1600 px JPEGs into slots 292–678 CSS px wide.
- WebP variants cut mobile load bytes by 58% under devtools throttling (313,000 -> 132,093 B) and by 65% under simulated throttling (423,715 -> 148

findings.title: Text contrast below WCAG 1.4.3 AA on every template: footer copyright in light mode; article links, primary buttons and footer in dark mode
findings.evidence:
axe-core 4.x (Playwright 390x844), 8 pages, light and dark: 57 color-contrast nodes. Lighthouse color-contrast fails in 16/16 runs.

Grouped by colour pair (axe-cc.js):
- .footer-bottom p, every page: #a0a0a0 on #f5f5f5 = 2.39:1 (light) and #606060 on #1a1a1a = 2.76:1 (dark), from --color-text-muted (tokens.css lines 33 and 113).
- Dark .article-body a / .article-toc a: #3377cc on #1a1a1a = 3.85:1 and on #232323 = 3.48:1. The dark theme maps --color-primary-dark to a darker blue (tokens.css line 118); components.css lines 1822 and 1964 use it for links. Counts: newest post 20 nodes, legacy post 11.

- Add `[data-theme="dark"] .btn-primary { background-color: #2a6fc9; }` (white 4.98:1) and `[data-theme="dark"] .btn-primary:hover { background-color: #1f5fae; }` (6.35:1).

The muted token is used in 11 rules (date/meta text, status dot); all get darker in light mode and lighter in dark mode, so there is no layout change.
findings.rollback: Revert the tokens.css and components.css commit.
findings.benefit: Removes the only WCAG AA contrast failures seen on all 7,047 pages and makes dark-mode article reading meet AA.

Dark mode is real-world traffic, not a toggle few people use: _layouts/default.html lines 23-37 set data-theme="dark" automatically from prefers-color-scheme when nothing is saved. findings.title: Assistant widget on every page: accessible name does not contain the visible label, and the modal dialog neither traps nor returns focus
findings.evidence:
axe and Lighthouse label-content-name-mismatch on 8/8 pages: `#assistant-toggle` has aria-label='Mở trợ lý hỗ trợ', but the visible text is 'Hỏi nhanh' (_includes/assistant.html line 6). Production shows the same 'Hỏi nhanh' label (TinyFish fetch of 3 live URLs).

Keyboard probe (kbd.js) on the newest post:
- After Enter on the toggle, focus moves to #assistant-input (good). aria-expanded=true, but aria-controls is null.
- After 14 Tab presses focus is on a background article link ('Báo Lào Cai', inPanel=false), although the panel declares role=dialog aria-modal=true.
- After Escape, focus stays on that background link instead of returning to the toggle.

assets/js/assistant.js togglePanel()/closePanel() have no focus trap or focus return.
findings.root_cause: The widget is marked as a modal dialog but implements only open/close class toggling.
findings.proposed_fix:
SAFE_TEMPLATE.

_includes/assistant.html:
- Change to `aria-label="Hỏi nhanh – mở trợ lý hỗ trợ"`, which starts with the visible text, or drop aria-label and keep the visible span.
- Add `aria-controls="assistant-panel"`.

assets/js/assistant.js:
- In closePanel(), and in the Escape and overlay handlers, call `this.toggleBtn.focus()` when the panel was open.
- Add a keydown Tab handler on this.panel that cycles focus between its first and last focusable elements, as in the APG modal dialog pattern.
- Alternatively, if a non-modal panel is preferred, remove aria-modal="true" so background content is not hidden from screen readers.

Verify: rerun kbd.js (focus stays inside the panel and returns to #assistant-toggle on Escape) and axe (label-content-name-mismatch = 0).

findings.title: 4-5 separate unminified render-blocking stylesheets on every page cost about 300-400 ms of mobile FCP (lab)
findings.evidence:
_layouts/default.html lines 13-22 load these as separate render-blocking files:
- tokens.css 3,082 B
- base.css 4,696 B
- components.css 53,893 B
- responsive.css 19,479 B
- editorial.css 3,278 B, on home and post layouts
- pricing-table.css 8,583 B, on pricing pages
Total 81-84 KB raw, 13.1-13.8 KB gz.

Lighthouse render-blocking-insight on the gzip server: 'Est savings of 340-390 ms' FCP/LCP on all 8 URLs. On python http.server, 570-725 ms mobile.

unused-css-rules flags 42-54 KB per page uncompressed. The gzip run passes that audit, so this is not the main lever.

Prototype with one bundle (same order, comments and whitespace stripped, 68,279 B raw / 10,257 B gz) plus deferred scripts: FCP went from 1,200-1,260 ms to 902-960 ms on home, /thue-xe/thue-thang/ and the newest post (2 runs each). Full-page pixel diff at 390 and 1280 px differs only in the logo and photo pixels, with identical page heights, so the cascade was preserved.

All non-home pages already score 100 in gzip lab, hence P3.
findings.root_cause: Stylesheets are authored as separate files and linked individually with no build-time concatenation.
findings.proposed_fix:
SAFE_TEMPLATE.
- Add assets/css/site.css with empty front matter (`---` / `---`) whose body is `{% include_relative tokens.css %}{% include_relative base.css %}{% include_relative components.css %}{% include_relative responsive.css %}`.
- Add assets/css/site-editorial.css with the same body plus editorial.css.
- In _layouts/default.html, replace the 4-5 links with one `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/css/site(.css|-editorial.css)?v=<date>">`. Keep pricing-table.css conditional as it is.
- Keep the original files, because 404.html and en/ pages may reference them.
- Do NOT pass the bundle through scssify or Sass. actions/jekyll-build-pages@v1 uses LibSass, which can choke on modern CSS (env(), :focus-visible, aspect-ratio). Plain concatenation already removes 3-4 round trips; minification can be a later step.

Verify: screenshot diff on 8 URLs, rerun Lighthouse, quality-gate FULL.

Expected impact: about -300 ms lab mobile FCP on every page, 4 fewer requests.
findings.rollback: Restore the original <link> lines in default.html; the new bundle files become inert.
findings.benefit: Faster first paint on slow mobile connections for all 7,047 pages, with no visual change.
findings.verdict: Không qua phản biện (P3 — workflow chỉ phản biện P0–P2)
findings.next: Đợt 5 (sau khi đợt 4 live và có kết quả phản biện)

findings.title: 8.5 KB of inline JSON (pricing/business/assistant) is serialized into the <head> of 7,047 pages; the pricing part is used on only 2 pages
findings.evidence:
_layouts/default.html lines 41-45 inline window.NGUYEN_TU_PRICING (3,703 B), NGUYEN_TU_BUSINESS (2,045 B) and NGUYEN_TU_ASSISTANT (2,616 B). That is 8,486 B raw / 2,642 B gz per page, on 7,047 of 7,050 HTML files, about 59.8 MB raw across the build.

Who reads the globals (grep):
- PRICING: only calculator.js, which loads only on home and /bang-gia/ (2 pages in the build). assistant.js line 19 assigns this.pricing but never reads it.
- BUSINESS and ASSISTANT: assistant.js, only when a question is answered.
- WhatsApp link: calculator.js.

All three scripts initialise on DOMContentLoaded or a readyState check (main.js lines 371-375, calculator.js tail, assistant.js tail). main.js, assistant.js and calculator.js are at end of body without defer.

Prototype:
- PRICING kept inline only where calculator.js loads.
- BUSINESS and ASSISTANT moved to a deferred site-data.js (4,722 B raw / 1,873 B gz, cacheable).
- defer added to main, assistant and calculator.
Result: newest-post HTML 17,738 B gz became 15,416 B gz (-13%). The assistant 'Địa chỉ' answer was identical ('112 Nguyễn Văn Cừ, Bồ Đề, Long Biên, Hà Nội, Việt Nam'), the calculator WhatsApp href was identical, and there were 0 console errors.
findings.root_cause: Data globals are emitted unconditionally in the shared layout instead of next to their consumers.
findings.proposed_fix:
SAFE_TEMPLATE, in two steps.

Step A (zero-risk):
- In _layouts/default.html, wrap the NGUYEN_TU_PRICING line in the same condition as calculator.js: `{% if page.layout == 'home' or page.url == '/bang-gia/' %}`. Assign it once as `needs_calc` and reuse it for both.
- Remove the unused `this.pricing` from assets/js/assistant.js.
- Saves 3.7 KB raw / about 1.1 KB gz on 7,045 pages.

Step B:
- Create assets/js/site-data.js with empty front matter and the body `window.NGUYEN_TU_BUSINESS = {{ site.data.business | jsonify }}; window.NGUYEN_TU_ASSISTANT = {{ site.data.assistant | jsonify }};`.
- Load it with `<script defer src=...site-data.js>` before main.js, and add defer to main.js, calculator.js and assistant.js. Deferred scripts run in document order before DOMContentLoaded, so consumer order is preserved.
- Keep the inline theme-init script (it must run before paint).
- Business data stays sourced only from _data/business.yml.

Verify with a functional test (assistant quick answers, calculator, theme toggle, mobile menu) and with check-built-links.
findings.rollback: Restore the inline <script> block and remove the defer attributes.
findings.benefit: About 1.1 KB gz per page from Step A, about 2.3 KB gz per page from Steps A+B. Less HTML for crawlers to fetch on 7k+ pages, and the data becomes cacheable across navigations.
findings.verdict: Không qua phản biện (P3 — workflow chỉ phản biện P0–P2)
findings.next: Bước A xong (JSON giá chỉ ở 2 trang). Bước B (dữ liệu business/assistant ra tệp defer) — đợt sau.

findings.title: Liquid loops without whitespace control: 106.7 MB of blank lines in 804 MB of HTML; listing pages are 76-77% whitespace
findings.evidence:
Scan of 7,050 HTML files: 804.1 MB total, of which 106.7 MB (13.3%) is blank lines.

Examples:
- /thue-xe/: 312,116 B, 77% whitespace, 26,655 blank lines. 24,755 of them are in one run after the 'Bài viết mới trong chủ đề' post-grid, from the `{% for post in site.posts %}` loop in _layouts/hub.html lines 40-56.
- Worst pages are the 711 /trang/N/ listings, e.g. thue-xe/thue-thang/trang/8: 366,827 B raw becomes 85,860 B with blank lines removed (15,756 to 12,265 B gz, -22%).

_layouts/topic-listing.html has 0 `{%-` tags; hub.html has 3, topic.html has 5.

Uncompressed transfer made /thue-xe/ the slowest mobile page on python http.server (FCP 3,007 ms). With gzip it is 100/1,208 ms, so this is mostly crawl bytes and artifact size.
findings.root_cause: Loop bodies emit newlines and indentation for every skipped iteration over all ~6,250 posts.
findings.proposed_fix:
SAFE_TEMPLATE.
- Convert loop and condition tags to whitespace-trimming form (`{%- for ... -%}`, `{%- if ... -%}`, `{%- assign ... -%}`, `{%- endif -%}`, `{%- endfor -%}`) in _layouts/topic-listing.html, _layouts/hub.html (lines 17-56) and _layouts/topic.html.
- Rendered DOM text and links must stay identical. Verify with a normalized-whitespace diff of built pages before and after, plus check-built-links and check-site-urls.
- Build time is unaffected. The O(N) loops themselves are a separate build concern (see SEO-103 / build-performance.md).
findings.rollback: Revert the layout commit.
findings.benefit: About 100 MB smaller Pages artifact and 15-22% fewer gzip bytes on 711 listing pages and the hubs. Less raw HTML for Googlebot to fetch on high-link-value listing pages.

findings.title: Floating phone and assistant buttons can fully cover the keyboard-focused element on mobile: scroll-padding is set on body instead of html
findings.evidence:
base.css lines 179-186 set `body { scroll-padding-bottom: calc(76px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) }` inside @media (max-width: 767px). Scroll padding only affects the viewport when it is set on the root element.

Keyboard probe (kbd2.js, 390x844), tabbing until the footer:
- /thue-xe/: 40 focus stops, 2 partially and 1 FULLY obscured ('Liên hệ') by the fixed #phoneLauncher (56x56) and #assistant-toggle (122x44) at bottom 768-828 px.
- /kinh-nghiem/: 1 partially obscured.
- Newest post: 2 partially obscured.

Injecting `@media (max-width:767px){html{scroll-padding-bottom:calc(76px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px))}}` reduces fully obscured stops to 0 (WCAG 2.4.11 minimum met).

The footer already has bottom padding; the full-page screenshot shows the 'Về đầu trang' button clear of the widgets.
findings.root_cause: The CSS property is placed on the wrong element.
findings.proposed_fix: SAFE_TEMPLATE. In assets/css/base.css (mobile media block, about line 181), change the selector `body` to `html` for scroll-padding-bottom. Keep the .site-footer padding rule. Verify with kbd2.js on 4 pages.
findings.rollback: Change the selector back.
findings.benefit: Keyboard users on phones and tablets no longer lose the focused link under the floating CTAs (WCAG 2.2 AA 2.4.11). The change is one line.
findings.verdict: Không qua phản biện (P3 — workflow chỉ phản biện P0–P2)

findings.title: Minor semantic issues: FAQ headings skip h2 to h4 on 8 static pages; footer logo alt repeats the adjacent brand text

Verify: axe heading-order and image-redundant-alt = 0; check-built-links and faq_parity_check PASS.
