findings.title: Non-issues to avoid re-raising: compression/cache audits are localhost artifacts; CLS, TBT, tap targets, overflow, SEO and Best Practices are clean
findings.evidence:
These Lighthouse failures come from the local server, not the site:
- uses-text-compression and document-latency-insight ('Est savings 123-204 KiB') fail only on python http.server, which sends no gzip. Live GitHub Pages compresses, and the gzip mimic passes.
- uses-long-cache-ttl and cache-insight reflect the fixed GitHub Pages `max-age=600`, which a static Pages site cannot change.

Measured clean on all 8 URLs (axe UX probes and Lighthouse):
- CLS 0.0001-0.0133.
- TBT 0-84 ms.
- No horizontal overflow at 390 px (scrollWidth = 390). The off-screen mobile menu and assistant chips are hidden.
- Lighthouse target-size passes. The sub-24 px items are inline text links, exempt under WCAG 2.5.8.
- System font stack only (no webfont cost).
- service-card images have CSS aspect-ratio (no CLS).
- SEO 100 and Best Practices 100 in all 16 runs.
- Live TinyFish check: production serves the same template (H1, 'Hỏi nhanh' toggle, footer).
findings.root_cause: Lab environment limits plus the GitHub Pages hosting model.
findings.proposed_fix: NO_ACTION. Do not add caching or compression workarounds or a service worker. Report lab numbers only alongside the gzip-mimic results, and validate any improvement with field data once GSC/CrUX is connected (SEO-109).
findings.rollback: N/A
findings.benefit: Keeps the backlog focused on the real levers (home images, CSS, contrast, assistant a11y).

dimensions.summary: I inventoried every in the existing build of HEAD a7aaedfc (7,050 HTML files) and every deployed raster image. There are 21,147 tags. Of these, 21,141 are the same 512x512 logo (/IMG_2536.jpeg), three per page (header, mobile menu, footer) on 7,047 pages. The other 6 are on the homepage (hero plus 5 service cards). The 6,257 posts have 0 content images. Basic image hygiene is clean: 0 images without an alt attribute, 0 with empty alt, 0 keyword-stuffed alts and 0 broken src. The likely LCP image (desktop hero) is not lazy-loaded and has fetchpriority=high. The below-the-fold cards are lazy, and their CSS aspect-ratio containers keep CLS at 0.0001. The real problems are with the image files and the image metadata: (1) Six deployed JPEGs carry the same GPS EXIF tag (21.0388N, 105.8536E, stamped 2025-12-15 09:58:53). Five are white-background catalogue photos and one is the unreferenced Air Blade photo. The point is in Hoàn Kiếm, not at the verified Long Biên address, and Google does not use EXIF anyway. A lossless strip is pixel-identical. (2) Two root images are deployed but never referenced: "Honda air blade.jpeg" (128 KB, carries GPS) and "Logo moto.png". (3) og:image and twitter:image are the 512px logo, which contains text, on all 7,047 pages. BlogPosting.image is that logo on 6,257 posts. No page sets max-image-preview. All of this goes against Google's "avoid site logo / image with text" guidance and the Discover rule of at least 1200px. Real vehicle photos (1200x800 / 1600x900) that show the right vehicle type exist for 11 vehicle hub and price pages. (4) The homepage serves 102–132 KB, q93 JPEGs with no srcset. Lighthouse estimates savings of 261 KiB on mobile and 518 KiB on desktop. Images are 54% / 65% of the bytes transferred. (5) The logo is 28 KB, 30% of it EXIF, and is shown at 40–48px. The footer logo alt duplicates the text next to it. Posts are recorded as IMAGE PENDING: real photos must come from the owner, and no images were generated. Live checks with TinyFish (1 call) confirmed og:image and twitter:image are the logo on / and /xe-may/honda-vision/, with no robots meta. The root images still appear to be served: they returned empty_content, the same result as the known-live logo, while missing URLs return 404. Inputs reused read-only: the sibling Lighthouse 12.8.2 JSONs in audit/performance-a11y/lh. Google docs came from Parallel web_fetch, because WebFetch cannot resolve developers.google.com in this session. My outputs are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-blog/c0138ac4-51ee-5beb-a1c9-21d2311d0295/scratchpad/audit/image-seo/: img_inventory.py, img-occurrences.csv, pages-summary.csv, summary.json, image-files.json, strip_sim.py, sim/strip-sim.json and thumbs/sheet.jpg. Overlap with other dimensions: BlogPosting.image (structured-data) and image-redundant-alt (performance-a11y) may also be reported there, so dedupe at merge.

findings.title: Same GPS EXIF tag added after the fact to 6 deployed JPEGs (5 homepage catalogue photos + root Air Blade); point does not match the verified address
findings.evidence: FACT (PIL getexif GPS IFD, image-files.json): assets/images/services/xe-so-honda-wave.jpeg, xe-tay-ga-honda-vision.jpeg, xe-50cc.jpeg, xe-dap-dien.jpeg and the root 'Honda air blade.jpeg' all carry exactly the same GPS values: GPSLatitude 21°2'19.74"N, GPSLongitude 105°51'12.98"E, GPSDateStamp 2025:12:15, GPSTimeStamp 09:58:53, GPSHPositioningError 1.0. xe-50cc.jpeg's own DateTimeOriginal is 2023:09:05 (Photoshop 22.0 XMP), so the GPS was stamped more than 2 years after the image was made. The photos are white-background catalogue cutouts (contact sheet thumbs/sheet.jpg), which cannot share one GPS fix taken at the same second. The 5 service photos are served on the homepage (hero + cards). INFERRED: 21.03882N, 105.85361E is on the Hoàn Kiếm / Old Quarter side, west of the Red River. The only verified address (data/business-facts.json) is 112 Nguyễn Văn Cừ, Bồ Đề, Long Biên, on the east bank. So these coordinates are unverified location data that conflicts with the NAP. Repo rules forbid fake geo coordinates and mixing in data from other businesses. Google (Search Office Hours, January 2023): 'Google doesn't use EXIF data for anything at the moment. The only image … metadata that we currently use is IPTC.' So geotagging brings no SEO benefit and only adds risk. FACT: the lossless simulation (strip_sim.py → sim/strip-sim.json) removes the APP1/APP13 segments, pixels stay identical in 7/7 files and no GPS remains. Savings: 372 B per file, 3,314 B for xe-50cc and 8,451 B for IMG_2536.jpeg.
findings.root_cause: The images were run through a geotagging tool (an outdated local-SEO tactic) before they were committed.
findings.proposed_fix: Strip all EXIF, XMP, IPTC and Photoshop metadata (APP1, APP13, COM) without recompression. Keep the APP0/APP14 segments and the entropy-coded data. Keep the same filenames and URLs for: assets/images/services/xe-so-honda-wave.jpeg, xe-tay-ga-honda-vision.jpeg, xe-50cc.jpeg, xe-dap-dien.jpeg, IMG_2536.jpeg, and 'Honda air blade.jpeg' if it is not excluded under IMG-02. Commands: `exiftool -all= -overwrite_original <file>` or `jpegtran -copy none -optimize`, both lossless; the marker-stripper in strip_sim.py also works. Verify: PIL pixel diff = none, getexif().get_ifd(0x8825) is empty, and URLs and file names are unchanged. That keeps og:image and the favicon URL stable, as Google's favicon guideline requires. Optionally add a tiny guard (e.g. scripts/seo/check-image-metadata.py) that fails when any deployed JPEG has a GPS IFD. If the owner later wants credit or licence data, add IPTC Creator/Credit/Copyright deliberately per Google's image-license-metadata documentation. Do not put coordinates in EXIF; location stays in the verified-NAP LocalBusiness markup.
findings.rollback: git revert the asset commit; it restores the original bytes at the same paths.
findings.benefit: Removes unverified location data that contradicts the verified NAP, removes needless metadata (about 8 KB from the logo loaded on every page), and keeps pixels and URLs unchanged.
findings.verdict: IMPLEMENT_WITH_CHANGES: The problem is real, but the auditor overcounted it: 5 files carry GPS, not 6, and IMG_2536 has no GPS at all. All 5 GPS files share one GPS stamp, which cannot be a real per-photo capture. The stamp's date is 2025-12-15, while xe-50cc was made on 2023-09-05. The coordinate is not in data/business-f

findings.title: Two unreferenced root images deployed publicly: 'Honda air blade.jpeg' (128 KB, GPS, filename with spaces) and 'Logo moto.png'
findings.evidence: FACT: the build root has 'Honda air blade.jpeg' (127,954 B, 1200x800, carries the GPS EXIF from IMG-01) and 'Logo moto.png' (27,486 B, 512x512, an alternative app-icon logo). grep across all git-tracked files (including 6,257 _posts, _data/*, _layouts, _includes, assets/css, assets/js, assets/data/webmcp-index.json and search-recent.json) finds 0 references to 'air blade.jpeg', 'air%20blade', 'Logo moto' or 'Logo%20moto'. findings.title: og:image/twitter:image is the 512px text logo on all 7,047 pages; 11 vehicle hub/price pages have matching real photos available but don't use them
findings.evidence: FACT (summary.json): og:image = twitter:image = https://blog.thuexemaynguyentu.com/IMG_2536.jpeg on 7,047/7,047 pages, with og:image:width/height 512 and twitter:card=summary_large_image. Live TinyFish confirms this on / and /xe-may/honda-vision/. The logo contains the text 'Thuê Xe Máy Hà Nội / NGUYỄN TÚ'. Google (google-images, 'Specify a preferred image'): 'Avoid using a generic image (for example, your site logo) or an image with text in the schema.org markup or og:image meta tag … Use a high resolution'. Discover: at least 1200 px wide, more than 300,000 px, 16:9, 'Avoid using generic images (for example, your site logo)'. 0 pages declare an image of 1200px or wider. FACT: assets/images/services holds real catalogue photos already published on the homepage, with alts set in _data/business.yml: Honda Vision (1200x800), Honda Wave (1200x800), 50cc (1200x800), electric scooter (1600x900) and electric bicycle (1200x800). Each meets the 1200px / 300K px threshold. Each matches the subject of these pages: /xe-may/honda-vision/, /xe-may/xe-ga/ and /bang-gia-xe-ga/ (Vision); /xe-may/honda-wave/, /xe-may/xe-so/ and /bang-gia-xe-so/ (Wave); /xe-may/xe-50cc/ and /bang-gia-xe-50cc/ (50cc); /xe-may/xe-dien/ and /bang-gia-xe-dien/ (electric scooter); /xe-may/xe-dap-dien/ (electric bicycle). These hubs currently show no image at all (topic.html and page.html contain no ). /xe-may/honda-air-blade/ is excluded: the only Air Blade photo shows an older-generation model and is unreferenced, so the owner must confirm it is representative. UNKNOWN: the licence or rights for these catalogue-style photos; the homepage caption already says 'Hình tham khảo từ danh mục xe'.
findings.root_cause: _includes/seo.html hard-codes business.logo as the only og:image and twitter:image source, and the hub layouts have no image slot.
findings.proposed_fix: (1) New non-business data file _data/page-images.yml, keyed by page.url, e.g. "/xe-may/honda-vision/": {vehicle: "Xe tay ga", w: 1200, h: 800}. Add the 11 URLs listed in the evidence. The vehicle names reference _data/business.yml vehicle_types, so src and alt keep a single source. (2) _includes/seo.html: `{% assign pimg = site.data.page-images[page.url] %}{% if pimg %}{% assign pv = site.data.business.vehicle_types | where: 'name', pimg.vehicle | first %}{% endif %}`. When pv is set, output og:image = pv.image | absolute_url, og:image:width/height = pimg.w/pimg.h, og:image:alt = pv.image_alt, twitter:image = the same plus twitter:image:alt. Otherwise keep the logo, unchanged. (3) _layouts/topic.html, after the page-description paragraph, and _layouts/page.html, after the lead: when pv is set, render `` with the existing caption 'Hình tham khảo từ danh mục xe. Tình trạng xe cần xác nhận khi liên hệ.' Do not lazy-load it, since it may be in the first viewport. Add the IMG-06 srcset derivatives once they exist. No .md file under _posts and no URL changes. Verify: rebuild; check-regressions stays 9/9 (homepage untouched); the 11 URLs show the vehicle og:image and a visible figure; every other page still has the logo og:image. Precondition: the owner confirms the right to use the catalogue photos; they are already live on the homepage.
findings.rollback: Delete _data/page-images.yml, or revert the three template edits. Pages fall back to the logo exactly as today.
findings.benefit: The 11 commercial vehicle hubs get a relevant, at least 1200px preferred image that is eligible for text-result thumbnails, Discover-sized previews and Google Images, plus better social share cards, without making up any photo.
findings.verdict:
IMPLEMENT_WITH_CHANGES: (a) The issue is real and correctly counted, re-measured independently (see corrected_measurement). The site-wide og:image is a 512px square logo with text, and with summary_large_image it is cropped on X/Twitter.

(b) Current guidance supports the change. Google's "Specify a preferred image with me
findings.next: Phản biện: cần chủ xác nhận quyền dùng 5 ảnh xe (ảnh danh mục, có thể của hãng) làm ảnh chia sẻ trước khi đặt og:image cho 11 trang xe/bảng giá. Template đã hỗ trợ page.image.

findings.title: No page opts into max-image-preview:large (Discover large-image prerequisite)
findings.evidence: FACT: a robots meta tag exists only on 404.html and tim-kiem/index.html (page.robots noindex). The 7,045 sitemap URLs have no max-image-preview directive. Live / and /xe-may/honda-vision/ show no robots meta (TinyFish page_metadata). Google robots meta spec: 'If you don't specify the max-image-preview rule, Google may show an image preview of the default size'. Discover: large images must be 'Enabled by the max-image-preview:large setting, or by using AMP'.
findings.root_cause: The template only prints a robots meta tag when a page sets robots explicitly.
findings.proposed_fix: _includes/seo.html: keep `{% if page.robots %}<meta name="robots" content="{{ page.robots }}">{% else %}<meta name="robots" content="max-image-preview:large">{% endif %}`, so the 2 noindex pages stay byte-identical. Ship it together with or after IMG-03 so at least 11 pages have a large image to preview. Verify: the 7,045 indexable pages carry the tag; noindex pages unchanged; check-regressions 9/9.
findings.rollback: Remove the else branch in _includes/seo.html.
findings.benefit: Lets Google show large image previews in Search and Discover once representative images exist. It is a permission-only directive with no indexing effect.
findings.verdict: Không qua phản biện (P3 — workflow chỉ phản biện P0–P2)
findings.next: max-image-preview:large trên trang không có page.robots

findings.title: 6,257 posts have no content image; BlogPosting.image and og:image are the logo (IMAGE PENDING)
findings.evidence: FACT (img_inventory.py): 0 tags inside the content or main area on any of the 6,257 article pages. The only images are the 3 logo tags from the header, mobile menu and footer. The JSON-LD 'image' key with the logo appears 13,304 times: 7,047 LocalBusiness + 6,257 BlogPosting. Google Article documentation: 'The URL to an image that is representative of the article. Use images that are relevant to the article, rather than logos or captions … Images must represent the marked up content.' FACT (research/keyword-serp-2026-10-31.json): the only tracked query where the blog ranks in the top 10, 'thuê xe máy phố cổ hà nội' (organic #4), has an 'images' SERP feature. The ranking page is the legacy post /du lịch/2026/09/19/thue-xe-may-quan-hoan-kiem-gan-pho-co/ (_posts/2026-09-20-thue-xe-may-quan-hoan-kiem-gan-pho-co.md, no article_id, 1 of 483 legacy posts that can be edited directly). It has no image that could compete there. There are no image-generation tools, and business photos must not be fabricated.
source_files: _posts/2026-09-20-thue-xe-may-quan-hoan-kiem-gan-pho-co.md (legacy; only with an owner-supplied real photo)
findings.root_cause: The content pipeline produces text-only posts and has no verified photo library or image field in the post schema.
findings.proposed_fix: Record every post as IMAGE PENDING. The owner should supply real, rights-cleared photos: shop, actual fleet, and real route photos for the cung-duong and du-lich posts. Do not use stock photos presented as the shop's own, and do not use AI 'business' photos. Priority order: (a) the legacy Phố Cổ post above, which can be edited directly as a legacy post: one real photo with descriptive Vietnamese alt, width/height, and an `image:` front-matter field. (b) For NEW factory posts, extend the writer schema to accept optional `image` and `image_alt`; this needs factory validate.py support and owner approval. (c) Published factory posts only through scripts/factory/revise-published.py with --approval-ref. Template follow-up (SAFE_TEMPLATE, can ship now): in _includes/seo.html, use page.image for og:image, twitter:image and BlogPosting.image when it is set. When page.image is absent, drop the logo from BlogPosting.image (Organization.logo still identifies the publisher). Use twitter:card 'summary' instead of 'summary_large_image' when the fallback is the square logo. This is INFERRED: X crops large cards to about 2:1, which cuts the logo text.
findings.rollback: Template: revert _includes/seo.html. Content: remove the image front matter or block from the edited legacy post.
findings.benefit: Real images make posts eligible for image results, Discover and text-result thumbnails on the one query where the blog already ranks. Dropping the logo from BlogPosting removes markup that goes against Google's Article guidance.

findings.title: Homepage serves 1200–1600px q93 JPEGs with no srcset/sizes; images are 54% of mobile / 65% of desktop bytes
findings.evidence: FACT (img-occurrences.csv): the homepage has 6 : the hero (xe-so-honda-wave.jpeg, width=640 height=480, fetchpriority=high, decoding=async, not lazy) and 5 service cards (loading=lazy, decoding=async, no width/height). None has srcset/sizes or . Files are 1200x800 or 1600x900, JPEG quality 92–93 (ImageMagick %Q), 102,572–132,405 B each, 552,139 B for the 5. FACT (Lighthouse 12.8.2 home-mobile.json and home-desktop.json, read-only from audit/performance-a11y/lh): mobile uses-responsive-images est. 261 KiB, modern-image-formats 221 KiB, uses-optimized-images 73 KiB; desktop 518 / 310 / 95 KiB. Image transfer is 374,395 of 687,949 B on mobile (54%) and 581,423 of 894,977 B on desktop (65%). LCP is the hero img on desktop (845 ms; markup correct) and p.hero-subtitle text on mobile (4,057 ms). CLS is 0.0001, because CSS aspect-ratio (16/10 cards, 4/3 hero with object-fit:cover) reserves space. FACT (sim/strip-sim.json): resized WebP q80 totals 68,902 B at 480w (-87.5%) and 132,880 B at 800w (-76%) for the 5 photos.
findings.root_cause: home.html prints the single full-size business.yml image path and no responsive variants exist.
findings.proposed_fix: (1) Add derivative files next to the originals; do not touch the originals' URLs: assets/images/services/-480.webp and -800.webp. Optionally add -480.jpg / -800.jpg q82 progressive as a fallback. (2) _layouts/home.html, hero: ``. Keep the alt and no lazy. Set width/height to the intrinsic 1200/800, since CSS still crops to 4:3. (3) Service cards: the same pattern with sizes matched to the grid columns (e.g. "(max-width: 768px) 100vw, 33vw"), keep loading=lazy, and add width="1200" height="800" (1600x900 for xe-may-dien). Check the sizes values against the breakpoints in assets/css/responsive.css. The original JPEG stays as the src fallback, as Google recommends. Verify: rerun Lighthouse on home mobile and desktop and confirm the responsive-image and format savings are near 0 and CLS stays ≤0.01; check-regressions 9/9 (hero text, H1, title and meta are not touched).
findings.rollback: Revert _layouts/home.html. The derivative files are inert if unreferenced and can stay or be deleted.
findings.benefit: About 200–450 KB less per homepage view (mobile/desktop), so less bandwidth competes with render-critical CSS on the main commercial page. It also adds the width/height hygiene web.dev recommends.
findings.verdict: CHƯA PHẢN BIỆN — agent phản biện lỗi do giới hạn sử dụng 5 giờ của tài khoản (31/10/2026 ~19:10 UTC)

findings.title: Site-wide logo: 512px / 28 KB JPEG (30% EXIF thumbnail) displayed at 40–48px on every page
findings.evidence: FACT: /IMG_2536.jpeg is 512x512, 28,139 B, quality 64. It contains an 8,391 B APP1 EXIF block with an 8,107 B embedded thumbnail (identify -verbose), and its XResolution is NaN. It is rendered by 3 tags per page on 7,047 pages (header 44x44 attributes, CSS 40px; mobile menu 40; footer 48). Lighthouse flags it on all 16 audited runs (8 page types × mobile/desktop): uses-responsive-images est. 27 KiB, modern-image-formats est. 14 KiB. Simulated: lossless EXIF strip gives 19,688 B (-30%); a 96x96 WebP q85 is 1,792 B and a 96x96 JPEG q85 is 2,544 B. The same file is og:image, Organization.logo, LocalBusiness.image, rel=icon and apple-touch-icon. Google requires a stable favicon URL, so the file must not be renamed despite its generic camera filename.
findings.root_cause: The header and footer reuse the 512px social/favicon asset for a 40–48px display.
findings.proposed_fix: (a) Covered by IMG-01: lossless metadata strip of IMG_2536.jpeg, same URL. (b) Add a display-size derivative, assets/images/logo-96.webp (or a .jpg fallback), generated from IMG_2536.jpeg. Point only the three visual tags in _includes/header.html (lines 8 and 97) and _includes/footer.html (line 9) at it, keeping width/height 44/40/48. The path can be hard-coded in the includes or put in a new non-business _data/branding.yml; do not change business.yml. Keep business.logo (IMG_2536.jpeg) for og:image, JSON-LD, the favicon and apple-touch-icon. Verify: Lighthouse uses-responsive-images and modern-image-formats pass on non-home pages; visual check in light and dark theme.
findings.rollback: Revert the src in _includes/header.html and _includes/footer.html; the derivative file is inert.
findings.benefit: About 26 KB less on every first page view across all 7,047 URLs, and the Lighthouse image audits clear on posts and hubs.
findings.verdict: Không qua phản biện (P3 — workflow chỉ phản biện P0–P2)

findings.title: Logo alt text repeats link text: footer alt duplicates the adjacent brand name; header/mobile links are named twice
findings.evidence: FACT (img-occurrences.csv and _includes): header `Nguyễn Tú` uses a redundant aria-label plus alt. In the mobile menu, the link has no aria-label, so its computed name is 'Thuê Xe Máy Hà Nội Nguyễn Tú Nguyễn Tú'. In the footer, img alt 'Thuê Xe Máy Hà Nội Nguyễn Tú' is followed by span.brand-name with the same text. Lighthouse image-redundant-alt fails on the footer logo in 16/16 runs. This affects 7,047 pages × 3 images. Google uses image alt as anchor text for image links, and the logo image literally reads 'Thuê Xe Máy Hà Nội – NGUYỄN TÚ'.
findings.root_cause: The templates set the full display_name as alt even though visible text or an aria-label already names the same link.
findings.proposed_fix: _includes/footer.html line 9: alt="" (the brand-name span already carries the full name). _includes/header.html lines 8 and 97: alt="{{ business.display_name | remove: business.brand | strip }}" (renders 'Thuê Xe Máy Hà Nội'), and remove the aria-label on a.site-logo. Each homepage link then has the accessible name and anchor text 'Thuê Xe Máy Hà Nội Nguyễn Tú' exactly once. No new business data, only derived from business.yml. Verify: axe/Lighthouse image-redundant-alt passes; the link name in DevTools shows once. Overlaps with the performance-a11y dimension, so dedupe at merge.
findings.rollback: Revert the alt and aria-label edits in _includes/header.html and _includes/footer.html.
findings.benefit: Clean accessible names for screen readers, a Lighthouse a11y pass on every page, and the full anchor text to the homepage is kept.
findings.verdict: Không qua phản biện (P3 — workflow chỉ phản biện P0–P2)

findings.title: Checked and OK: alt coverage, broken src, LCP/lazy config, SVG icons, favicon, logo filename
findings.evidence: FACT (img_inventory.py over 7,050 HTML files): 21,147/21,147 have an alt attribute; 0 empty alts on non-decorative images; the longest alt is 28 characters, with no keyword stuffing; 0 broken src (all 6 distinct src resolve in the build); the desktop LCP hero has no loading=lazy and has fetchpriority=high; the 5 below-the-fold cards are lazy; 0 CSS background content images; 0 preload/picture misuse. Inline SVG icons on sampled pages (/, /bang-gia/, /xe-may/honda-vision/, /thue-xe/; 100–189 each) are all aria-hidden="true" focusable="false". Favicon: the 512x512 square JPEG meets Google's requirements (square, at least 8x8, more than 48 recommended, JPEG supported). assets/images/favicon.svg (664 B) is only an else-branch fallback, and Google's list of favicon formats does not include SVG, so keep the JPEG icon. The generic filename IMG_2536.jpeg gives Google only 'very light clues'; renaming would break the stable favicon/og/Organization.logo URL. assets/minima-social-icons.svg (9,906 B) is an unreferenced theme-gem asset. An image sitemap is not needed: no content images, and all images are discoverable as . Optional for the owner: a simpler square mark (e.g. the pin/motorbike symbol) would read better at 16–32px than the logo with text, but that is a brand decision.
findings.root_cause: n/a
findings.proposed_fix: No change. Keep the IMG_2536.jpeg URL stable. Monitor in future audits so new templates keep alt, width/height and a non-lazy LCP image.
findings.rollback: n/a
findings.benefit: Documents the checks that passed, so later waves don't redo them.

dimensions.dimension: crawl/index hygiene — sitemap, robots, URL formats, duplicates, special pages
dimensions.summary:
Crawl and index hygiene on HEAD a7aaedfc is in good shape. I compared sitemap.xml with the 7,050 built HTML files, the noindex pages, the slug-d stubs, 404, /tim-kiem/, feed.xml and sitemap-core.xml (scripts in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-blog/c0138ac4-51ee-5beb-a1c9-21d2311d0295/scratchpad/audit/crawl-index/).

What checks out (FACT): the sitemap's 7,045 <loc> match the 7,045 indexable built pages exactly. That means 0 sitemap URLs missing from the build, 0 duplicates, 0 noindex or stub URLs in the sitemap, 0 canonical≠loc, 0 query strings, 0 URLs without a trailing slash. The 5 built pages left out of the sitemap are all intended: /404.html and /tim-kiem/ (noindex,follow) plus 3 meta-refresh stubs. The slug registry checks out: all 1,405 RETIRED old URLs are gone from the build, the 3 MIGRATED stubs are present, and all 1,408 new URLs are in the sitemap. robots.txt allows everything and lists the sitemap. Nothing leaks from _drafts (0 built). Of 653,639 internal hrefs, none point to /index.html, a URL missing its trailing slash, http://, the www host or an unresolved target. og:url and hreflang equal the canonical on every page, and every page has exactly one H1. The 711 pagination pages are all self-canonical with unique 'Trang N' titles. Thin content is limited to 5 last pages of topic listings; every post has at least 585 words.

The one real issue (P2): 254 factory posts were corrected through revise-published.py on 2026-10-23..27 (price, legal and deposit fixes). Their sitemap <lastmod> and BlogPosting dateModified still show the original publish date. The tool never writes last_modified_at.

Smaller issues (P3, NEW): (a) 231 topic-listing pages share the site-default meta description. (b) 46 raw non-ASCII/space hrefs in 30 factory posts disagree with the percent-encoded canonical/sitemap form; the 483 legacy URLs themselves stay frozen. (c) No page has a feed autodiscovery link, and the feed holds only 10 posts while about 50 are published per day. (d) sitemap-core.xml is a stale 9-URL hand-made duplicate: deployed, but not referenced anywhere.

The live checks agree with the local build: http redirects to https; the www host does not exist; the live sitemap has 7,048 URLs (a newer deploy than HEAD); canonicals match on 5 sampled pages. The SEO-107 pagination keep decision and the /tim-kiem/ noindex are confirmed with new evidence.

findings.title: 254 posts fixed via revise-published.py still show their original publish date as sitemap <lastmod> and BlogPosting dateModified
findings.evidence: FACT: there are 11 backups in reports/qa-audit/revise/*.json (2026-10-23..27: price-01..05, legal-01..04, deposit-02, A01), covering 254 distinct article_ids. Mapped by article_id to the current _posts file and compared with site-base/sitemap.xml, 254/254 have <lastmod> older than their last revise (lag 3–30 days, median 8). Examples: BLG-01632 lastmod 2026-10-07 vs revised 2026-10-23 (deposit-02); BLG-01903 2026-10-10 vs 2026-10-23 (legal-01). `grep last_modified_at scripts/factory/*.py` returns 0 hits, so revise-published.py never sets it. Only 4/6,257 posts have last_modified_at in front matter. jekyll-sitemap and _includes/seo.html:170 (dateModified) both use page.last_modified_at|date. Visible date (_layouts/post.html:51) shows only page.date. INFERRED, same problem: about 40 legacy posts edited directly (SEO-108/110/119/121 in fix-log.csv) and 90 posts that gained price or legal notice blocks. Full list: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-blog/c0138ac4-51ee-5beb-a1c9-21d2311d0295/scratchpad/audit/crawl-index/revised-posts-stale-lastmod.csv
findings.root_cause: The revise-published maintenance path changes main content (prices, legal citations, deposit wording) but keeps the front matter date untouched for evidence-hash reasons. No other mechanism sets last_modified_at.
findings.proposed_fix:
SAFE_TEMPLATE, does not touch _posts bytes or evidence SHA:
(1) _config.yml: add a `defaults:` block generated from the CSV, one scope per revised file. Example: `- scope: {path: "_posts/2026-10-07-khach-quoc-te-tra-xe-ngoai-gio-nen-bo-tri-ra-sao.md"}` with `values: {last_modified_at: 2026-10-23 20:30:50 +0700}`, the date taken from the backup's created_at. None of the 254 has front-matter last_modified_at, so no override conflict. jekyll-sitemap and the seo.html dateModified then pick it up.
(2) _layouts/post.html line 51: after the publish date, add `{% if page.last_modified_at %} · Cập nhật {{ page.last_modified_at | date: "%d/%m/%Y" }}{% endif %}` so the visible and structured dates match.
Verify on a local build: 254 sitemap <lastmod> equal the revise date, JSON-LD dateModified is identical, check-regressions 9/9, check-built-links PASS, and Jekyll build time is not materially worse.
NEEDS_OWNER follow-ups: revise-published.py should append to this list on future applies; legacy direct edits need dates from a full git clone.
findings.rollback: Remove the generated defaults block from _config.yml and the 'Cập nhật' line from _layouts/post.html; the sitemap and JSON-LD return to page.date.
findings.benefit: Google uses <lastmod> only when it is consistently accurate. Accurate lastmod for the 254 corrected price, legal and deposit pages encourages faster recrawl of the corrected facts, and keeps dateModified truthful.
findings.verdict: CHƯA PHẢN BIỆN — agent phản biện lỗi do giới hạn sử dụng 5 giờ của tài khoản (31/10/2026 ~19:10 UTC)
findings.next: dateModified + dòng "Cập nhật" xong (254 bài). Sitemap <lastmod> cần last_modified_at front matter hoặc _config defaults — đợt sau.

findings.title: All 231 topic-listing pages share the site-wide default meta description
findings.evidence: FACT: links_pass.py over the build finds one duplicate meta-description group covering 231 URLs. That is exactly every layout:topic-listing page, each using 'Kinh nghiệm thuê xe máy Hà Nội, chọn xe, du lịch, bảng giá và hướng dẫn di chuyển từ Nguyễn Tú.' (site.description), which also feeds og:description and twitter:description. The 480 category listing pages are unique ('Các bài viết X, trang N/M.'). scripts/factory/generate-listing-pages.py writes `description:` for category pages (line ~93) but not in the topic branch (lines ~113-118); listing/topic/hoi-dap/hoi-dap-phap-ly/2.md has no description. Titles are already unique. List: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-blog/c0138ac4-51ee-5beb-a1c9-21d2311d0295/scratchpad/audit/crawl-index/topic-listing-default-description.csv
findings.root_cause: The generator omits description for topic listings, so seo.html falls back to site.description.
findings.proposed_fix: SAFE_TEMPLATE in _includes/seo.html. Before the description meta, compute one variable: `{% assign seo_desc = page.description %}{% if seo_desc == nil and page.layout == 'topic-listing' %}{% capture seo_desc %}Các bài viết {{ page.title | split: ' - ' | first }}, trang {{ page.page_num }}/{{ page.total_pages }}.{% endcapture %}{% endif %}`. Then use `seo_desc | default: page.excerpt | default: site.description` in the three description/og/twitter tags. Pages with a description, including the frozen homepage, are unaffected. Alternative (NEEDS_OWNER, factory engine): add the same description line to the topic branch of generate-listing-pages.py. Verify: duplicate-description groups go to 0; check-regressions H1 confirms the homepage meta is unchanged.
findings.rollback: Revert the _includes/seo.html change.
findings.benefit: Gives 231 sitemap URLs unique, accurate descriptions, matching the category listings.
findings.verdict: Không qua phản biện (P3 — workflow chỉ phản biện P0–P2)

findings.title: 46 internal links in 30 factory posts use raw non-ASCII paths with literal spaces instead of the percent-encoded canonical form
findings.evidence: FACT: of 5,839 internal hrefs to legacy encoded URLs, 46 hrefs on 30 pages (BLG-00520..00539, 00597, 00629..00634, 00648..00652, 06120) pointing at 15 targets are written raw, e.g. href="/kinh nghiệm/2026/09/18/checklist-kiem-tra-xe-khi-nhan-xe-thue/" on /thue-xe/2026/09/27/dat-coc-khi-thue-xe-may-hoat-dong-the-nao/. The sitemap <loc>, canonical, og:url and hreflang use '/kinh%20nghi%E1%BB%87m/...' (483/483 uppercase hex, 0 loc≠canonical). Source is kramdown links in _posts, e.g. line 35 of the BLG post above. All 46 are NFC, the non-ASCII part is only the prefix 'kinh nghiệm' (32) or 'chia sẻ' (14), and the rest of each path is ASCII. Browsers and Googlebot resolve them to the same URL; check-built-links passes. List: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-blog/c0138ac4-51ee-5beb-a1c9-21d2311d0295/scratchpad/audit/crawl-index/raw-nonascii-hrefs.csv
findings.root_cause: Factory drafts written in late September linked legacy posts by their decoded paths. Kramdown emits the href verbatim, with a literal space.
findings.proposed_fix: SAFE_TEMPLATE, render-time only. _posts bytes, URLs and evidence are unchanged; this follows the existing '//">' normalisation precedent. In _layouts/post.html line ~85, extend `post_body_html = art_content | replace: '//">', '/">'` with `| replace: 'href="/kinh nghiệm/', 'href="/kinh%20nghi%E1%BB%87m/' | replace: 'href="/chia sẻ/', 'href="/chia%20s%E1%BA%BB/' | replace: 'href="/du lịch/', 'href="/du%20l%E1%BB%8Bch/'`. Verify: raw non-ASCII href count goes to 0; check-built-links PASS; check-site-urls frozen=483 unchanged; diff limited to the 30 pages.
findings.rollback: Remove the three added replace filters from _layouts/post.html.
findings.benefit: One exact URL string per legacy page across links, canonicals and the sitemap, as Google's URL-structure guidance recommends (percent-encode non-ASCII in href). Avoids invalid-URL warnings from validators.
findings.verdict: Không qua phản biện (P3 — workflow chỉ phản biện P0–P2)

findings.title: 483 legacy URLs with encoded spaces and diacritics: keep frozen (encoding is already consistent)
findings.evidence: FACT: the sitemap contains 483 legacy URLs under '/du%20l%E1%BB%8Bch/', '/kinh%20nghi%E1%BB%87m/' and '/chia%20s%E1%BA%BB/'. All are uppercase-hex percent-encoded and identical to their canonical, og:url and hreflang (0 mismatches). This matches the check-site-urls.py frozen non-ASCII count of 483. The SERP snapshot (research/keyword-serp-2026-10-31.json) shows the blog's only top-10 result is a legacy URL: /du%20l%E1%BB%8Bch/2026/09/19/thue-xe-may-quan-hoan-kiem-gan-pho-co/ at #4 for 'thuê xe máy phố cổ hà nội'. It has 11 internal links, all encoded. Live fetch of /du%20l%E1%BB%8Bch/2026/09/13/goi-y-kham-pha-ha-noi-bang-xe-may-cho-nguoi-moi/ returns that same URL as final_url and canonical.
findings.root_cause: Legacy category names became the permalink path.
findings.proposed_fix: Do not change these URLs or their canonicals. GitHub Pages cannot issue 301s, and Issue #77 plus AGENTS.md forbid it. The only safe hygiene is CRAWL-03 (encoding the 46 raw links). Keep the check-site-urls frozen=483 ratchet.
findings.rollback: N/A
findings.benefit: Protects the one URL that currently ranks and avoids 404/soft-redirect churn.

findings.title: sitemap-core.xml is a deployed, hand-made 9-URL duplicate that nothing references
findings.evidence: FACT: /home/user/blog/sitemap-core.xml has 9 <url>, no <lastmod>, and is not in _config.yml exclude. It is built (site-base/sitemap-core.xml, 722 B) and live (TinyFish: final_url same, title 'Sitemap (9 URLs)', Last-Modified Sat 31 Oct 2026 17:22:29 GMT). robots.txt lists only /sitemap.xml and there is no sitemap index. `grep -rn sitemap-core` over scripts/docs/data returns 0 hits. All 9 URLs, /bai-viet/ included, exist in the build and are already in sitemap.xml. It omits the 6 hubs, 56 topic hubs and 3 category pages. Whether it is submitted in Search Console is UNKNOWN (GSC not connected).
findings.root_cause: A legacy manual sitemap left over from before jekyll-sitemap took over.
findings.proposed_fix: Owner decision. (a) If it is not submitted in GSC, or not wanted: delete it or add it to _config.yml `exclude:`, and remove it from GSC if listed. (b) If a 'core pages' monitoring sitemap is wanted once GSC is connected: generate it from the hub, topic and page front matter (about 77 URLs, with accurate lastmod) and add a second `Sitemap:` line in robots.txt. Listing a URL in two sitemaps is allowed.
findings.rollback: Restore the file from git.
findings.benefit: Removes a stale artefact, or turns it into a useful per-section coverage report in GSC.
findings.next: Chờ chủ website quyết định (xem báo cáo wave4)

findings.title: Atom feed has no autodiscovery link, and its 10 posts cover only a fraction of daily output
findings.evidence: FACT: site-base/feed.xml is valid Atom with 10 entries and 114,115 B. All links are absolute https URLs and all 10 are in sitemap.xml; it is live (Last-Modified 17:22:30 GMT). 0 of 7,050 pages have a `<link rel=alternate type=application/atom+xml>`: _layouts/default.html has no `{% feed_meta %}`, and _config.yml has no `feed:` settings, so posts_limit is the default 10. Output: 48 posts are dated 2026-10-31 and 52 dated 2026-10-29, so the feed shows about 5 hours of output. robots.txt does not list the feed. INFERRED: since GSC is not connected, the feed's only discovery paths are autodiscovery or robots.txt.
findings.root_cause: The custom default layout never included the jekyll-feed meta tag, and the default limit was never tuned.
findings.proposed_fix:
SAFE_TEMPLATE:
(1) _layouts/default.html: add `{% feed_meta %}` inside <head> right after `{% include seo.html %}`.
(2) _config.yml: add `feed:` with `posts_limit: 50`. Feed size goes to about 0.6 MB (INFERRED); add `excerpt_only: true` if size matters.
(3) Optional: in robots.txt add `Sitemap: https://blog.thuexemaynguyentu.com/feed.xml`; Google accepts Atom 1.0 as a sitemap for recent URLs.
Verify: the feed link appears in the head on all pages; feed.xml has 50 entries; check-regressions 9/9; the homepage title, meta and H1 are unchanged.
findings.rollback: Remove the feed_meta tag, the feed: block and the robots.txt line.
findings.benefit: Faster discovery of new posts through a lightweight recent-URL feed, alongside the 1.27 MB full sitemap.
findings.verdict: Không qua phản biện (P3 — workflow chỉ phản biện P0–P2)

findings.title: Pagination and thin content: new evidence supports SEO-107 DECIDED_KEEP
findings.evidence: FACT: the sitemap has 711 pagination URLs (480 category /trang/N/ and 231 topic /trang/N/; up from 689 at SEO-107). All 711 are self-canonical, and all 711 titles are unique and contain 'Trang N'. There are no /trang/1/ duplicates of hubs and no head rel=prev/next, which Google does not need. Main-content words: listing min 197 / median 602; topic-listing min 53 / median 1,069. Pages in the sitemap under 150 words: only 5 topic-listing last pages with 1–3 cards (/xe-may/xe-dap-dien/trang/4/ 53, /du-lich/pho-co/trang/5/ 55, /hoi-dap/hoi-dap-gia/trang/3/ 129, /thue-xe/su-co/trang/9/ 138, /an-toan-phap-ly/giay-to/trang/5/ 143). Other templates: posts min 585 (p10 1,047), hubs ≥855, topic hubs ≥1,383, static pages ≥520, /chu-de/ 631. Duplicate <title> groups: 0.
findings.root_cause: N/A: the implementation follows Google's pagination guidance.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the SEO-107 decision: no noindex, no canonical-to-page-1, keep pagination in the sitemap. The 5 thin tail pages are a natural result of pagination and need no action. Revisit when GSC indexing data exists.
findings.rollback: N/A
findings.benefit: Confirms crawl paths to all 6,257 posts stay intact without self-inflicted indexing loss.

findings.title: Sitemap, special pages, slug stubs, drafts and internal links are consistent; close the /tim-kiem/ NOINDEX item as intended
findings.evidence: FACT (compare.py, links_pass.py): the sitemap's 7,045 <loc> match the 7,045 indexable built pages (0 missing, 0 extra, 0 noindex, 0 meta-refresh, 0 canonical mismatch). The 7,050 built files are those 7,045 plus /404.html (noindex,follow, sitemap:false), /tim-kiem/ (noindex,follow, sitemap:false, 122 words, client-side search UI) and 3 redirects/slug-d stubs (meta refresh 0, canonical to the new URL, sitemap:false). Slug registry: 1,405 RETIRED old URLs not built, 3 MIGRATED stubs present, 1,408/1,408 new URLs in the sitemap. robots.txt is 'User-agent: * / Allow: /' plus the Sitemap line, identical live and local. /tim-kiem/ is not robots-blocked, so its noindex is seen. _drafts: 6 files, 0 built (5 are stale copies of already-published BLG-01294/01295/01464/02059/02348, plus 1 template). 653,639 internal hrefs: 0 to /index.html, 0 missing a trailing slash, 0 http://, 0 www, 0 unresolved; 4 go to slug stubs (already tracked by slug-stub-link-ratchet). og:url and hreflang equal the canonical on all 7,047 non-stub pages, each with exactly one H1.
findings.root_cause: N/A
findings.proposed_fix: No change. Update reports/factory/seo-master/technical-issues.csv: NOINDEX /tim-kiem/ (OPEN P1) becomes DECIDED_KEEP. It is an internal search UI with noindex,follow, left out of the sitemap, and correctly not blocked in robots.txt. Keep the 404 page noindex as is; GitHub Pages serves it with HTTP 404.
findings.rollback: N/A
findings.benefit: Confirms no crawl or index leakage and closes a stale P1 item.

findings.title: Live checks match the local build; one sitemap is fine at the 10K-post target
findings.evidence: FACT (one TinyFish fetch call, ttl 0): http://blog.thuexemaynguyentu.com/ ends at https://blog.thuexemaynguyentu.com/; the title equals the frozen local title. https://www.blog.thuexemaynguyentu.com/ failed with error invalid_url (host appears not to resolve; HTTP status UNKNOWN; 0 internal links point to www). Live sitemap.xml reports 7,048 URLs vs 7,045 locally: the deploy (Last-Modified 17:22:29 GMT) is newer than HEAD a7aaedfc, and the first 5,000 live URLs parsed are all in the local set. Live robots.txt is identical. Live canonical equals local canonical for /, /thue-xe/thue-thang/, the newest post /cung-duong/2026/10/31/cot-co-lung-po-o-a-mu-sung-noi-song-hong-chay-vao-viet-nam-di-xe-may-tu-lao-cai/, /kinh-nghiem/trang/2/ and the legacy /du%20l%E1%BB%8Bch/2026/09/13/... (5/5); no robots meta on any. feed.xml and sitemap-core.xml are served. The tool does not expose HTTP status codes, so 200 is inferred from the content returned. Capacity: 7,045 URLs / 1.27 MB is 14% and 2.5% of the 50,000 URL / 50 MB limits. INFERRED: at the 10K-post target the total is about 11–12K URLs, still one file.
findings.root_cause: N/A
findings.proposed_fix: No sitemap index needed. Monitor: split into a sitemap index only above about 40K URLs, or for per-section coverage once Search Console is connected (SEO-109). Re-run this audit's compare.py after each engine change.
findings.rollback: N/A
findings.benefit: Confirms production serving matches the build, with no host duplication.

dimensions.summary:
I checked the 12 researched keywords from the 2026-10-31 SERP snapshot, compared them with seo-matrix-config K01–K12 and the matrix primary_keyword field, and read the 7 pillars, all 56 child hubs and the legacy category pages. The source is the HEAD a7aaedfc build (site-base). I also did one live fetch via TinyFish (7 URLs) to compare titles and meta descriptions; they match the build.

Keyword roles:

posts.json was checked against data/content-taxonomy.json:
- child_id 'undefined': BLG-03649, 03651, 03652, 03653, 03654, 03655, 03657 (2026-10-15). Matrix child_id is C-THUE-TUAN.
- 'C-THUE-THUE-NGAY': BLG-00513, 00514. Matrix: C-THUE-NGAY.
- 'C-HD-NGUOI-MO': BLG-01591. Matrix: C-HD-NGUOI-MOI.
None of the 10 slugs appears in site-base/thue-xe/thue-tuan/, thue-ngay/ or hoi-dap/hoi-dap-nguoi-moi/ (including the /trang/N/ pages). They are reachable only through related links and /kinh-nghiem/ pagination. scripts/factory/publish-gate.py checks only that the front matter contains title/date/categories/description; it never compares child_id with the matrix row.
findings.root_cause: The writer front matter had a bad child_id. The gate does not cross-check it, and published front matter is locked by the QA evidence SHA (revise-published.py may change only body and description).
findings.proposed_fix:
Immediate fix, SAFE_TEMPLATE, no post edits:
- Add _data/child-id-overrides.yml: slug → child_id for the 10 posts, values taken from data/content-matrix.csv. Example: `tuan-on-va-thi-sat-hach-bang-lai-o-to-o-ngoai-thanh-ha-noi-thue-xe-may-di-lai-gi: C-THUE-TUAN`.
- Where templates resolve mychild, add `{% assign _ov = site.data.child-id-overrides[post.slug] %}{% if _ov %}{% assign mychild = _ov %}{% endif %}`: _layouts/topic.html, _layouts/hub.html (2 places), _layouts/topic-listing.html, _includes/related-articles.html, _includes/topic-directory.html, and _includes/article-breadcrumb.html (page.slug).
- Verify: the 10 posts appear in their hub listings, and check-built-links.py / check-regressions.py pass.
Engine follow-up, owner/engine maintainer (not done by writers): validate.py --scope chunk or publish-gate.py should fail when draft child_id is not in the taxonomy or differs from the matrix row. Add a regression test.
findings.rollback: Delete the overrides data file; the template branches are no-ops without it.
findings.benefit: Puts 10 posts back into their topic clusters and stops new posts from slipping out of hubs.
findings.verdict: CHƯA PHẢN BIỆN — agent phản biện lỗi do giới hạn sử dụng 5 giờ của tài khoản (31/10/2026 ~19:10 UTC)

findings.title: Cannibalization since 2026-10-23: 1 new key collision, 1 model-swap duplicate, 3 templated variant series
findings.evidence:
cannib_new.py: 181 posts dated after 2026-10-23, compared with all 6,257 posts on title bigram Jaccard ≥0.30 or SequenceMatcher ≥0.62. 22 candidates, read by hand.
(a) NEW matrix cannibalization_key collision 'gia thue honda wave theo tuan': BLG-06184 (2026-10-29, 'Thuê Honda Wave theo ngày 150.000đ, tuần 700.000đ hay tháng 900.000–1.200.000đ…') vs BLG-03561 (2026-10-15, 'Honda Wave chỉ niêm yết giá ngày 150.000đ…'). The older post's premise is out of date since the owner table of 27/10 publishes week and month prices; it already carries a price-notice. Neither post is in scripts/seo/cannibalization-leads.json or technical-issues.csv. Body 6-gram Jaccard 0.014.
(b) Model-swap same intent: BLG-05711 (10-24, 'Chở bố mẹ đi xem chèo, cải lương… bằng Honda Click…') vs BLG-05684 (10-20, 'Tối đi xem kịch, chèo, cải lương bằng xe máy thuê…'); 6-gram 0.004.
(c) Templated series with distinct bodies (6-gram ≤0.015) to monitor:
- 'Chở trẻ nhỏ bằng <xe>': BLG-06183 new, plus 03217, 03864, 03160
- 'xếp tuyến theo quận và giữ <đồ> phẳng': BLG-06098 new, plus 04139, 03652
- 'Nhược điểm của <model> khi thuê': BLG-06185 new, plus 02591, 02156, 02546
The other 14 candidate pairs were reviewed as distinct angles: 06093/04859, 06091/04858, 06121/05134, 06198/04537, 06192/04513, 06202/05157, 06112/04381, 06111/04352, 06114/04377, 06094/05485, 06167/04596, 06246/04142, 06225/04714, 06235/03460.
findings.root_cause: Refill batches vary the model or occasion of an existing intent. Gates G1–G9 compare cannibalization keys, not title templates.
findings.proposed_fix:
Data, SAFE_TEMPLATE (no post edits): in scripts/seo/cannibalization-leads.json add
- 'gia thue honda wave theo tuan': SAME_INTENT_MONITOR, lead BLG-06184 (current prices), basis 'BLG-03561 tiền đề cũ trước bảng giá 27/10'
- 'xem kich cheo cai luong bang xe may': SAME_INTENT_MONITOR, lead BLG-05684, member BLG-05711
Then run build-cannibalization-classification.py and build-topic-links.py so both pairs get two-way 'Cùng chủ đề' blocks. Add BLG-03561 to the SEO-115 title-bound list (content-fix-blocked.csv) for the owner, since its title is tied to old pricing.
Process (owner/coordinator): before staging a refill batch, reject topics whose normalised title differs from an existing title only by a model, vehicle or occasion token. This follows Google's scaled-content-abuse policy; no URL changes, no noindex, no merges.
findings.rollback: Remove the 2 entries and re-run build-topic-links.py.
findings.benefit: Signals the current-price post as the lead and prevents further template-swap duplicates.

findings.title: Content gap: only 2 real gaps; district and station listicles and '50cc không bằng lái' must not be added
findings.evidence:
gap.py (regex on titles/descriptions of 6,257 posts) against the SERP page types:
- Station/ga: 71 posts mention ga Hà Nội; BLG-00905 is the lead of group 37. Bến xe Gia Lâm: 'Xuống xe khách ở bến xe Gia Lâm…' (C-LONG-BIEN) plus 'Thuê xe máy khu vực Gia Lâm'. Covered.
- Cầu Giấy and Hà Đông: 48 and 44 posts. The SERP pages are 'Top N shops in district' listicles, which is local-commercial intent and a doorway risk for a shop at 112 Nguyễn Văn Cừ. Reject.
- '50cc không cần bằng lái': 5 same-intent posts. Over-covered; consolidate via KW-02.
- Monthly guides: 2 general + 20 audience posts. Covered.
- Thủ tục/giấy tờ: 7+ posts. Covered.
- Cheap rental: BLG-00415 legacy. Covered.
Real gaps:
(1) App-based or shared e-scooter rental vs shop rental. The SERP for 'thuê xe máy điện hà nội' shows izigo/XanhSM and VinFast pages; posts mentioning vinfast/xanh sm/izigo = 0. Battery-swap posts exist (6), but there is no comparison of app vs shop on battery swapping, licence by motor power, deposit and documents, or service area.
(2) 'Thuê xe máy điện 1 ngày bao nhiêu tiền' (izigo result in that SERP). BLG-00491 'Giá thuê xe máy điện ở Hà Nội' cannot answer it because pricing.yml and business-facts have xe máy điện day/week/month = null.
findings.root_cause: Owner price data for e-scooters does not exist; the topic universe has not yet absorbed the app-based e-mobility competitors that dominate this SERP.
findings.proposed_fix:
Owner and coordinator:
(1) Owner decides whether to publish xe máy điện and xe đạp điện rates in _data/pricing.yml and data/business-facts.json. Until then, no post may give an amount.
(2) Coordinator adds a small refill batch under data/factory/refill-batches/ (through G1–G9; no filler) of 2–3 distinct topics, child C-XE-DIEN:
- 'Thuê xe máy điện qua ứng dụng hay ở cửa hàng: khác nhau ở pin, đổi pin, giấy tờ và tiền cọc'
- 'Xe máy điện công suất bao nhiêu thì cần bằng A1: đọc công suất trên giấy đăng ký trước khi thuê'
- 'Đổi pin ở trạm hay sạc tại nơi ở khi thuê xe máy điện theo tuần'
Run the G-gates first: the second topic must not duplicate 'Bằng lái xe máy điện: cần giấy phép nào khi thuê' (C-GPLX).
Legal facts to verify from official sources before writing: Luật Trật tự, an toàn giao thông đường bộ 36/2024/QH15 Điều 59.1.a (đủ 16 tuổi điều khiển xe gắn máy) and Điều 57.1.a (A1: đến 125 cm3 hoặc động cơ điện đến 11 kW), already quoted in reports/factory/seo-master/legal-verification.json (vanban.chinhphu.vn docid=217295). The statutory definition of xe gắn máy (≤50 cm3, and the electric power threshold) and any other obligations must be re-checked against the official text. Third-party service facts (app names, battery policies) come only from their official pages; no competitor prices; neutral wording.
findings.rollback: n/a (no page change; a refill batch that fails gates is not staged)
findings.benefit: Covers the only uncovered sub-intents of the most winnable volume keyword without doorway or filler pages.
